proposals.northStar: A drone holds station over the Korengal at first light and the feed is indistinguishable from a real ISR downlink: the valley floor is irrigated cropland in resolvable furrows, the slopes are holly-scrub giving way to cedar in the draws and to raked scree and bare rock on the crests, snow caps the pole-facing high ground, the river is actual water with a moving specular glint and a wet gravel bar, and the low sun rakes EVERY surface so the texture you see is real micro-relief catching light, not paint. The literal reading of "more realistic" is total physical fidelity of the GROUND. The thesis: top-down orthographic kills parallax and silhouette, so the entire illusion of a photographed surface must be carried by lighting acting on real geometry and real per-material micro-normals — never by a painted bitmap. I throw away attempt-1's `albedo*(0.34+0.95*shade)` over a flat bake and replace it with a fragment-resolution material compositor: a per-landcover PBR atlas (albedo + detail-normal + roughness) blended by landclass/slope/altitude/wetness, lit by the reusable physical SkyState (sun+hemisphere+moon), grounded by terrain-scale cast shadows AND micro-scale ambient occlusion, specular where water and wet ground live, then ACES-tonemapped with a whisker of bloom. The dust palette and the welded contours stay sacred; the ground stops being a map of the valley and becomes a photograph of it.
proposals.whatMakesThis10x: Attempt-1 moved a flat painted hillshade onto the GPU and added a tint, a cast shadow, and fog — "the same map, but the sun moves." The concrete leap: (1) The albedo bake is DEMOTED from "the image" to one input among five. The fragment now composes color from a tiling per-material PBR atlas sampled at world scale, so at close zoom the ground RESOLVES into real scree grains, furrow ridges, scrub stipple, cedar canopy lobes, and gravel — it does not upscale into a smear. (2) Real surface normals: a detail-normal map per material is perturbed onto the heightmap normal, so the low sun rakes thousands of pebble/furrow-scale facets — this is the single thing that makes a top-down surface read as photographed rather than painted, and attempt-1 had zero of it. (3) Genuine ambient occlusion: a baked horizon-angle AO field darkens cliff bases, draw bottoms, and the inside of terraces — the contact darkening every orthophoto has and attempt-1 faked with one `0.5+0.5*n.z` term. (4) Real water: animated dual-normal specular on the river/ford with a sun glint that tracks the live sun and Fresnel sky reflection — not a sine-ripple brightness wobble. (5) Physical surface state from the sim clock/weather: snow ACCUMULATES by altitude×aspect×slope and MELTS back, ground DARKENS and gains specular when wet after rain and dries over hours, tracks gather dust. (6) ACES filmic tonemap + threshold bloom turns the linear-space lighting into the gamma-correct, slightly-blooming highlight rolloff of a real sensor — attempt-1 wrote raw clamped linear values. The result is transformation: a surface, not a chart.

techniqueStack.name: Material-ID + control textures (the data spine)
techniqueStack.what: terrain/foundation. Uploads the sim's own arrays as GPU textures so the fragment shader can recompose the surface instead of reading a pre-painted color.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Three uploads beside the existing 512² R32F height: (a) u_landId — 512² R8UI (gl.R8UI/RED_INTEGER/UNSIGNED_BYTE) of terrain.land, NEAREST, read with texelFetch + a 2x2 nearest-with-noise-jittered-sample to keep organic class edges (port topo.ts:178 dither into GLSL). (b) u_control — 512² RGBA8 packing slope (terrain.slope/2 clamped), conceal (canopy density), cover, and a free channel, LINEAR. (c) u_surfaceState — a small 256² RGBA8 the CPU rebakes on weather/clock change: R=snowDepth, G=wetness, B=dryTrackDust, A=spare; sampled LINEAR. All cache-resident, ~0.8MB total. This is the contract with the sim: render reads, never writes.
techniqueStack.costMs: upload ~1-2ms on terrain load only; per-frame sampling cost folds into the material pass below. SwiftShader: negligible (texelFetch is cheap).
techniqueStack.risk: R8UI integer textures need correct sampler type (usampler2D) — well within WebGL2 core, no extension. Mitigation: a unit test asserts texelFetch(landId)==terrain.land[i] for 64 sample cells, same discipline as the heightAt parity test.

techniqueStack.name: Per-landcover PBR material atlas (albedo + detail-normal + roughness)
techniqueStack.what: terrain surface — THE centerpiece. Gives every landclass a real tiling material (scree grains, furrowed cropland, scrub stipple, cedar canopy, river gravel, HESCO basket weave, rock) that resolves at close zoom.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: One 2048² (or 1024²) RGBA8 albedo atlas + one RG8 normal atlas (z reconstructed) + pack roughness into albedo.a, authored as ~16 tiles for the material GROUPS (rock/scree, grass/scrub, forest/orchard canopy, cropland/terrace furrow, riverbed gravel, mud/compound, hesco, snow, gravel, dry-wash). Generated DETERMINISTICALLY at load by a CPU bake (or a one-time offscreen GLSL pass) from FBM + worley — NOT shipped PNGs, so no asset pipeline and the seed contract holds. Sample at WORLD scale: uv = v_world / tileMeters (tileMeters≈8m, with a second octave at 2m mixed by ppm so the tile never visibly repeats). Map Land enum→atlas slot via a const int[26] LUT in-shader. Blend two neighboring materials across class edges using the jittered land sample to dissolve the 5m stairstep. Albedo seeded from sky.ts landColor() means the strategic-zoom color is byte-faithful to today; the atlas only adds high-frequency detail that fades in with ppm.
techniqueStack.costMs: 3-6ms on SwiftShader at close zoom (2-3 atlas taps + 1-2 normal taps per fragment). Mitigated by ppm-gating the second octave + normals so strategic/operational pay almost nothing. iGPU: <1ms.
techniqueStack.risk: Atlas bleed at tile seams + texture thrash. Mitigation: pad tiles, clamp per-tile in shader math (manual atlas addressing, no hardware wrap across tiles), and gate detail strength by clamp((ppm-0.5)/1.5) so the LEGIBLE strategic view is unchanged from the bake — legibility floor protected by construction.

techniqueStack.name: Detail-normal raking (the photoreal trigger)
techniqueStack.what: terrain surface — the one technique that converts a top-down painted look into a photographed one. The live low sun rakes pebble/furrow/canopy-scale facets.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Perturb the heightmap normal (the existing forward-difference normalAt) by the atlas detail-normal in tangent space: since the surface is near-planar in screen space, use a cheap world-up TBN (tangent=+x, bitangent=+y) and rotate the detail normal by the macro slope. n = normalize(macroN + detailStrength * vec3(dN.xy, 0)). detailStrength ramps with ppm and is per-material (scree high, cropland furrows directional along the contour using the macro gradient, water handled separately). Lighting (next item) then does the rest — a furrow lit from the side throws its own shaded face.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.5ms (one extra normalize + the atlas normal tap already counted). The visual payoff per ms is the highest in the whole stack.
techniqueStack.risk: Over-strong normals at noon could fight the flat-relief legibility rule. Mitigation: detailStrength scales with (1 - sun flatness) so noon stays calm; capped so micro-normal never inverts the macro form-light.

techniqueStack.name: Physical sun+sky+moon lighting in linear space
techniqueStack.what: atmosphere/terrain — replaces the scalar `0.34+0.95*shade` hack with a real (diffuse sun · shadow) + hemisphere-ambient + moon model in linear light, driven verbatim by the reusable SkyState.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Work in linear (atlas albedos authored linear or de-gamma'd once). L = albedo*(sunColor*sunI*NdotL*shadowVis*cloudVis + hemisphere(skyColor,groundColor; based on n.z and AO) + moonColor*moonFactor*NdotMoon*shadowVis) + spec. Hemisphere ambient = mix(groundColor, skyColor, 0.5+0.5*n.z) * skyI * AO — physically the sky-dome bounce, and it carries the night/overcast read. Keep sky.ts's single-fold weather rule intact (exposure carries weatherLightMult once). Re-anchor the strategic LOD to today's luma via the existing keyGain/formLightNW guards so noon never inverts.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~1ms. Pure ALU. SwiftShader fine.
techniqueStack.risk: Linear-space change shifts overall brightness vs the byte-faithful gate. Mitigation: a one-time calibration pass matches mid-gray luma at noon-clear to the attempt-1 frame (a numeric gate, not a vibe), then I'm free to diverge by daylight — the brief explicitly authorizes transformation away from parity.

techniqueStack.name: Baked horizon-angle ambient occlusion (HBAO-lite)
techniqueStack.what: terrain — the contact darkening every real orthophoto has: cliff bases, draw bottoms, terrace insides, the lee of boulders go dim. Attempt-1 had none (only a fake n.z term).
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Bake a 512² R8 AO field ONCE per terrain (CPU or a one-shot GLSL pass): for each cell, march the heightmap in 8-16 azimuths a few steps each, accumulate the max horizon elevation angle, AO = 1 - average(sin(horizonAngle)). This reuses the exact exponential-stride march already written for the cast-shadow pass, just omnidirectional and sun-independent. Sampled LINEAR in the main pass, multiplies the ambient (NOT the direct) term so shadows+AO compound correctly.
techniqueStack.costMs: bake ~30-80ms once on load (16 azimuths × 512²); zero per-frame beyond one texture tap. Acceptable as a load cost beside the existing relief bake.
techniqueStack.risk: Bake time on SwiftShader if done in GLSL. Mitigation: do it CPU-side in the worker that already builds terrain, or 8 azimuths; it's a one-time cost hidden behind the existing deploy loading bar (topo.ts already has bakeTerrainProgressive plumbing to reuse).

techniqueStack.name: Refined cast-shadow penumbra + contact hardening
techniqueStack.what: terrain — keep attempt-1's correct 56-step exponential sun-visibility march (a 780m ridge throws a multi-km dawn floor shadow) but upgrade the penumbra so the shadow edge softens with distance like a real sun, and harden the contact line.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Keep SHADOW_FRAG's march and the rebake-on-sun-motion FBO (the master-clock-made-literal sweep at time-warp). Change the output: instead of binary lit, store the penumbra factor AND a 'distance to occluder' so the main pass widens the soft edge with distance (PCF-like 3-tap on the R8 vis map scaled by ppm). Raise SHADOW_SIZE handling so the contact at a boulder/HESCO base stays crisp.
techniqueStack.costMs: unchanged from attempt-1: rebakes a few Hz, not per-frame. 3-tap PCF in main pass ~0.3ms.
techniqueStack.risk: Low — this is refining proven code. Determinism preserved (output is sun-angle-determined; the wall-clock rate-limiter only throttles, never changes the result at a pinned clock).

techniqueStack.name: Real specular water (river + ford) with animated normals
techniqueStack.what: water — replaces the sine-brightness 'ripple' with actual water: a tracking sun glint, Fresnel sky reflection, and two scrolling normal layers so the channel reads as flowing water in a drone feed.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: For Land.River/Ford/Footbridge-adjacent fragments: build a water normal from two scrolling FBM-normal layers advected along the river centerline direction (derive flow dir from the macro gradient / centerX). Blinn-Phong/GGX spec lobe toward sky.sunDir with high roughness→tight glint at low sun (the dawn glint is the marquee). Fresnel: mix water albedo with skyColor by pow(1-NdotV,5) — but V is straight down (ortho) so Fresnel is near-constant and tuned as a constant grazing term. Flow phase integrated from the sim clock (deterministic, freezes on pause), NOT wall clock.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.5ms, only on water fragments (early-out by landId). SwiftShader fine.
techniqueStack.risk: Ortho camera has fixed view vector → no parallax sparkle; glint could look static. Mitigation: animate the normal field (clock-driven) so the glint shimmers along the channel; cap brightness so a noon glint never blows out the tactical read over the river crossing.

techniqueStack.name: Altitude×aspect snow accumulation & melt
techniqueStack.what: terrain — physical snow that builds on high, pole-facing, low-slope ground and recedes, instead of attempt-1's static painted snow cap. Reads as a real Hindu Kush winter/spring.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: snowLine from sim (clock day-of-campaign + weather Snow). coverage = smoothstep(line, line+band, elev) * (1 - slope*k) * aspectBias(n) where aspectBias favors north/pole-facing (n.y<0 in this world frame). Blend the snow material slot (high albedo, low roughness, subtle sparkle normal) over the base. The u_surfaceState.R channel holds an integrated snowDepth the CPU advances from weather so a snowfall accumulates over game-hours and melts on a clear warm day — a function of the clock, fully deterministic.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.3ms (one mix + the snow atlas tap shared with the material pass).
techniqueStack.risk: Snow could bury terrain legibility on the crests. Mitigation: snow respects the AO/relief so form still reads; coverage capped below ridgelines used for LOS; it's a slow campaign-scale change, never a strobe.

techniqueStack.name: Wet-ground darkening + tracks dust (weather memory)
techniqueStack.what: terrain — after Rain the ground darkens, saturates, and gains a wet sheen, then dries over hours; vehicle tracks/roads gather pale dust in dry spells. The valley remembers its weather.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: u_surfaceState.G (wetness) drives: albedo *= mix(1, 0.7, wet) (wet darkens), roughness *= (1-0.6*wet) (wet = shinier → a broad low-sun sheen via the spec lobe), saturation *= (1+0.2*wet). Wetness pools toward low ground (reuse the localFloor field) so draws stay wet longest. Dust (B channel) lightens/desaturates Road/Track fragments in dry spells. CPU integrates both from weather.precip and clock — deterministic.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.3ms, folds into material+lighting math.
techniqueStack.risk: Wet sheen could over-specular into glare. Mitigation: clamp the wet spec contribution and gate by sunI so overcast/rain (when it's actually wet) has weak direct light anyway — physically self-limiting.

techniqueStack.name: ACES filmic tonemap + threshold bloom + dither
techniqueStack.what: post — the sensor look. Converts linear lighting to the gamma-correct highlight rolloff and gentle bloom of a real camera; attempt-1 wrote raw clamped linear and looked digital.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: After all lighting/grade, ACES-fitted tonemap (Narkowicz 3-line approx) in the terrain fragment (single full-screen pass, no extra target needed for tonemap). Bloom: a cheap separable 5-tap Gaussian on a half-res bright-pass FBO of the terrain (threshold ~0.85 luma), added back — gives the dawn glint and snow a soft halo. Final ordered-dither (Bayer 8x8) to kill 8-bit banding in the sky-ambient gradients on the dim slopes.
techniqueStack.costMs: tonemap+dither ~0.2ms; bloom adds 1 half-res pass + 2 blur passes ≈ 2-3ms on SwiftShader. Bloom is the first thing cut under budget (gate it off below a perf threshold).
techniqueStack.risk: Bloom is the budget risk + a legibility risk (could veil the HUD — but HUD is on the 2D layer ABOVE the GL canvas, so it's physically immune). Mitigation: bloom only on the GL terrain canvas, thresholded high so only true highlights bloom; HUD/units/contours untouched by construction.

techniqueStack.name: Deterministic procedural decoration in-shader (close-zoom vegetation hint)
techniqueStack.what: veg — at close zoom, scrub/forest fragments gain stippled canopy lobes and the cropland gains furrow rows IN THE MATERIAL, so the ground reads as vegetated without spawning 10k sprites. Complements (doesn't replace) the existing decoration.ts sprite scatter.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Use conceal (canopy density, from u_control) to modulate a worley-cell 'canopy lobe' pattern in the forest/orchard material (each cell a rounded bright/dark lobe lit by the sun dir → reads as 3D-ish tree crowns from above, the classic orthophoto forest texture). Cropland furrows = directional stripes along the macro contour (port topo.ts:207). All ppm-gated to close band.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.5ms, close-zoom only.
techniqueStack.risk: Could clash with the existing sprite trees fading in over the same band. Mitigation: this is the SUB-sprite-resolution texture; sprites fade in above it and the canopy texture fades UNDER them — author the crossfade so they're the same color family (already locked by palette).

techniqueStack.name: Terrain self-color bounce + aerial perspective (depth)
techniqueStack.what: atmosphere — the valley gains real aerial depth: distant/low ground hazes toward the sky color, and warm sunlit slopes bounce a faint warm fill into adjacent shadow, the way a real wide-valley drone shot does.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Keep + upgrade attempt-1's altitude haze (it's fine) but drive haze color from sky.skyColor (already graded) and add a screen-space cheap bounce: sample the cast-shadow vis of a neighbor toward the sun and add a small warm term to shadowed fragments adjacent to lit ones (a 2-tap on the vis map). Subtle.
techniqueStack.risk: Bounce is subtle and easily cut; lowest priority. Haze must not gray out the tactical read — keep attempt-1's low-altitude-only falloff.

techniqueStack.name: Crisp 2D layer stays the tactical instrument
techniqueStack.what: post/legibility — NOT a render technique but the architectural guarantee: contours, units, fire reticles, labels, HUD all stay on the transparent Canvas-2D layer ABOVE the GL canvas, ungraded and pixel-crisp.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: No shader. Preserve the two-canvas skeleton from terrain-gl.ts (opaque GL under transparent 2D, DPR + shake sync). drawContoursLive/drawPathsLive stay 2D vectors welded to the same heightmap. drawScreenGrade uses source-atop so it never veils the GL showing through.
techniqueStack.costMs: 0 (existing path).
techniqueStack.risk: None — this is the legibility firewall that lets the GL layer 'go wild' safely.

proposals.theOneHolyShitMoment: Dawn, operational zoom, looking down the river draw. The sun sits ~6° above the eastern ridge. A 780-m spur throws a kilometres-long blue-shadowed apron across the valley floor (the proven cast-shadow march) — but where the light DOES land, it rakes the surface: the scree fields on the lit west-facing slopes erupt into thousands of tiny pebble-shadows (detail-normals catching the low sun), the cedar in the draws reads as clumped 3-D canopy lobes, the irrigated cropland on the floor shows furrow rows running along the contour, snow on the pole-facing crests catches the first warm light while their north faces stay blue, and down the centre the river is ACTUAL WATER — a specular sun-glint travels along the channel as the flow normals scroll, with the wet gravel ford glinting beside it. Pull the camera into close zoom on that ford and the ground RESOLVES — gravel, wet darkening, individual scree grains — instead of smearing into an upscaled bitmap. The whole frame is ACES-tonemapped with a faint bloom on the glint and snow. The skeptic who watched Restrepo says 'that's a real ISR feed.' It is produced by exactly four stacked techniques firing at once: the cast-shadow march (the macro shadow), detail-normal raking under the physical low sun (the surface erupting), specular water (the glint), and altitude×aspect snow (the cold crests) — none of which attempt-1 had.
proposals.legibilityPlan: The legibility firewall is architectural, not negotiated per-effect: contours, units, reticles, labels, and HUD live on the transparent 2D canvas ABOVE the GL layer and are never touched by any shader (legibility contract #1, #2 satisfied by construction). Per band: STRATEGIC (ppm≤0.35) — detail-normals, the material atlas's second octave, bloom, and procedural decoration are all ppm-gated to ~0; the view collapses to the byte-faithful albedo+relief+contours of today, calibrated to match attempt-1's noon luma numerically, so the strategic map is provably unchanged. OPERATIONAL (0.35–1.2) — material detail and AO fade in gently; terrain SHAPE still dominates because direct-sun relief + cast shadow + AO are all form-revealing, not form-hiding. TACTICAL (1.2–3) — full materials + normals; structures stay legible because the HESCO/compound materials use the locked built-material palette and the 2D building sprites sit on top. CLOSE (>3) — full surface resolution is the GOAL here, not a risk. Noon guard (contract #3): the formLightNW relief-inversion blend is kept, detail-normal strength scales DOWN as the sun flattens, and the linear-light calibration gate forbids relief inversion or washout — verified numerically, not by eye. Fog/weather floor (contract #4): the atmosphere veil is alpha-capped (reuse sky.ts's single-fold rule) and never pushes terrain below the legibility luma floor; HUD is immune anyway. Determinism (contract #5): every animated term (water flow, cloud drift, snow/wetness state) integrates from the sim clock and freezes on pause; only screen-space precip uses wall clock; the surface-state texture is a pure function of (clock, weather, seed). The whole stack is verified with the recovered matrix tool across 4 bands × times × weathers before it's called done.
phasePlan: Phase 0 — Re-establish the skeleton green. Restore the reusable sky.ts, atmosphere-model.ts, terrain-gl.ts, shaders.ts and the two-canvas WorldView wiring as the LIVING baseline (attempt-1's lit shader, parity look). Confirm tsc/build/lint/smoke/balance green and capture the 4-band×time×weather matrix as the 'before' reference. Game playable and identical to attempt-1.

Phase 1 — Linear lighting rebuild. Rewrite the terrain fragment to light in linear space (sun diffuse·shadow + hemisphere ambient + moon) from SkyState, then ACES tonemap. NO new textures yet — albedo still the bake. Calibrate noon-clear mid-gray luma to attempt-1 numerically (the one parity gate I keep). Commit: 'feat(render): linear-space terrain lighting + ACES tonemap'. Matrix re-shot; relief must not invert at noon.

Phase 2 — The data spine. Upload landId (R8UI), control (slope/conceal/cover), and the surfaceState texture. Add the const Land→material LUT and the jittered class-edge blend. No visible change yet beyond dissolved 5m stairsteps. Unit test: texelFetch parity vs terrain arrays. Commit: 'feat(render): material-ID + control textures'.

Phase 3 — THE material atlas + detail normals (the centerpiece). Deterministic CPU/one-shot bake of the albedo+normal+roughness atlas; world-scale sampling, ppm-gated detail strength, per-material detail-normal raking. This is where the surface starts to read as photographed. Commit: 'feat(render): per-landcover PBR material atlas + detail-normal raking'. Matrix shot at CLOSE band — the make-or-break frame.

Phase 4 — Grounding: HBAO bake + cast-shadow penumbra refine. Bake the 512² AO field (reuse the march), wire it into the ambient term, soften the shadow penumbra with distance. The contact darkening lands. Commit: 'feat(render): baked horizon AO + softened cast-shadow penumbra'.
Phase 5 — Water. Specular river/ford with scrolling clock-driven normals, sun-tracking glint, Fresnel sky reflect. Commit: 'feat(render): physical specular water'. This is the second marquee element.

Phase 6 — Surface state physics. Altitude×aspect snow accumulation/melt + wet-ground darkening + track dust, all integrated from clock/weather into surfaceState (deterministic; added to serialize/loadWorld if persisted). Commit: 'feat(render): physical snow/wetness/dust surface state'.

Phase 7 — Post polish + decoration. Threshold bloom (budget-gated), Bayer dither, in-shader canopy/furrow texture, aerial-perspective bounce. Commit: 'feat(render): bloom, dither, procedural surface micro-detail'. Final full matrix; publish the HTML report with before/after at every band.
Each phase ends with tsc/build/lint/smoke/balance green and a matrix re-shoot; the game is playable and better-looking at every commit, never broken mid-stack.
proposals.riskiestBet: The riskiest bet is detail-normal raking carrying the close-zoom photoreal read on a TOP-DOWN ORTHO camera. The whole illusion rests on the low sun lighting micro-normals into visible facets; but at noon (sun near-vertical, due south) NdotL is near-uniform across all micro-facets, so the surface can flatten back toward 'painted' exactly when the player most needs detail, and an over-strong normal can fight the macro form-light and read as noise rather than rock. Mitigation/fallback: (1) detailStrength is per-material and scales with sun rake-angle, so noon leans on albedo+AO+roughness micro-contrast rather than normals — it degrades to 'a very good textured orthophoto' rather than failing. (2) If SwiftShader can't afford the atlas+normal taps at close zoom in the headless harness (the honest cost worry), the fallback is a single-channel detail HEIGHT map turned into normals on the fly (one tap, derivatives) plus a roughness-driven micro-contrast term — cheaper, still reads as surface, just less material-specific. (3) The absolute floor: even if normals are cut entirely, Phases 1+3 (linear lighting + world-scale material albedo + AO) already beat attempt-1 decisively, because the ground stops being a single upscaled bitmap and becomes resolving per-material texture — so the 10x is not all-or-nothing on the riskiest technique. Bloom is the other cut candidate and is isolated to one gateable post pass.

proposals.northStar: The map is not a map — it is a frame of *Restrepo* B-roll a drone shot at the moment the light decided to tell you what time it is. Attempt-1 painted a hillshade bitmap and tinted it; that is a photograph of a relief model under a colored gel. We do the opposite: throw away "albedo × shade" entirely and rebuild the renderer as a small physically-motivated light-transport pipeline in LINEAR HDR, tonemapped by real ACES at the very end. Light is computed, not painted — a warm direct beam the color sky.ts already knows, a cool hemispheric sky-fill that doubles as ambient occlusion, a moon key at night, all in radiance units that can legitimately exceed 1.0 so snow crests and river glints actually BLOOM. Over the lit ground we lay the three things that make documentary mountain footage feel like air and distance: aerial perspective (the valley floor recedes into haze-blue because there is literally 2 km of dusty atmosphere between the high crest and the river), raymarched valley fog that pools in the river draw at dawn and burns off by mid-morning, and — the money shot — volumetric light shafts: at blue-hour the sun rakes between the ridgelines and god-rays fan across the fog in the draws, sampled from the SAME cast-shadow map the relief uses, so the shafts are geometrically TRUE to the ridge that throws them. Then a film finish: bloom on highlights, a time-of-day color grade that is a real tonemap-and-balance not a wash, fine grain, a breath of vignette, a hair of lateral chromatic aberration at the corners. The whole thing is driven by sky.ts and the master clock, so dawn is amber and low and foggy, noon is flat and high and clear, dusk goes long-shadowed and golden, and 02:00 is a blue scotopic hush with a hard little moon. Realism strictly in service of MOOD: every technique earns its place by making the light tell the time and the weather, and every one of them is clamped above the legibility floor so the soldier reading the ground never loses the read.
proposals.whatMakesThis10x: Attempt-1 was `col = bakedAlbedo * (0.34 + 0.95*shade)` then a tint `fillRect`. Three concrete leaps past that: (1) RENDERING MOVES TO LINEAR HDR. We bake a flat un-lit, un-shaded LINEAR albedo (delete every lighting/haze/altitude term currently baked INTO topo.ts — those become live shader math), light it per-fragment in radiance that exceeds 1.0, and resolve through real ACES-fitted tonemapping in a final fullscreen pass. This single change is why attempt-1 looked like gouache and this looks like film — there is no tonemap in attempt-1, so highlights clip flat and shadows crush; with ACES the dynamic range of golden hour becomes legible and the grade has a real signal to work on. (2) ATMOSPHERE BECOMES LIGHT TRANSPORT, not a darkening mix(). Attempt-1's fog/haze are `mix(col, fogColor, t)` — paint. We replace them with single-scattering aerial perspective (extinction + inscatter integrated over the air column between crest and floor, tinted by the sun) and a short raymarch through the fog volume that accumulates in-scatter from the sun beam — which produces actual GOD-RAYS in the draws at low sun, the marquee shot attempt-1 never even attempted. (3) THE GROUND GROWS REAL SURFACE + REAL WATER. Triplanar-free, normal-mapped detail materials per landcover class synthesized procedurally at close zoom (scrub catches a soft anisotropic sheen, scree gets micro-relief self-shadow, snow sparkles), and the river stops being a baked blue stripe with a sine ripple — it gets a real water shader: animated normal-perturbed surface, Fresnel sky reflection, and a sun-glitter specular streak that blooms. Plus the assets get relit by the same SkyState (a one-pass screen-space directional relight of the sprite layer) so a B-hut at dusk is lit amber from the west and shadowed cool to the east, instead of wearing its baked noon shading at 19:00. Net: the same valley, but it is now MADE OF LIGHT AND AIR, photographed, and graded — not painted and tinted.

techniqueStack.name: Linear-HDR pipeline + ACES tonemap (the foundation)
techniqueStack.what: Post — converts the entire renderer from 8-bit paint to physically-meaningful radiance. Everything below assumes it. Without it, golden hour clips and bloom looks like haze.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Render terrain into an RGBA16F FBO (half-float color attachment; SwiftShader supports EXT_color_buffer_half_float / WebGL2 core RGBA16F renderable). Bake albedo SRGB→linear on upload (pow 2.2 or sRGB sampler). All lighting math in linear, radiance allowed >1. Final fullscreen pass: ACES fitted curve (Narkowicz `(x*(2.51x+0.03))/(x*(2.43x+0.59)+0.14)` as the cheap path; Hill RRT/ODT 3x3 fit as the quality path), then linear→sRGB OETF. Exposure from sky.grade.exposure feeds the tonemap input scale (single-fold rule preserved). This is one extra fullscreen triangle reading the HDR target.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.4ms @ 1080p on SwiftShader (one fullscreen pass, ALU-light; the FBO half-float bandwidth is the real cost, ~8MB target). iGPU: negligible.
techniqueStack.risk: Half-float renderable under SwiftShader is the load-bearing assumption — MITIGATION: probe `RGBA16F`+`COLOR_BUFFER_HALF_FLOAT` at init; if absent, fall back to RGBA8 with a packed-exposure trick (render at /2 exposure, ×2 in tonemap) which loses some highlight range but keeps the pipeline shape. Legibility: ACES gently desaturates extreme highlights — keep noon exposure ≤1.0 so the relief never blows out (contract #3).

techniqueStack.name: Recomputed PBR-ish relief lighting (delete the baked shade)
techniqueStack.what: Terrain — replaces attempt-1's `albedo*(0.34+0.95*shade)`. The albedo bake (topo.ts) is stripped to FLAT linear landcover color only; all directional light, fill, AO, altitude-tint, haze move into the live shader driven by SkyState. This is what makes noon vs dusk a real lighting difference, not a tint.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Reuse the bit-faithful `normalAt` (keeps contour registration). Diffuse = sunColor*sunI*max(0,N·sunDir)*castVis*cloudVis*sunUp (in radiance). Sky-fill = (skyColor*upHemi + groundColor*downHemi)*skyI where upHemi=0.5+0.5*N.z doubles as cheap AO. Moon as second key at night (moonColor*moonFactor*N·moonDir*castVis). Energy stays in linear; the warm sun beam can push lit snow >1.0 to feed bloom. Keep the NW-key form-light blend (`u_formLightNW`) ONLY as a noon anti-inversion guard (contract #3), not as the primary light.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.6ms (4-tap height for normal + light math, screen-res). Same draw call as attempt-1, more ALU. iGPU negligible.
techniqueStack.risk: Low — this is attempt-1's structure made honest (radiance not 0-1, albedo flat not pre-lit). MITIGATION for contract #3: clamp the sky-fill floor so shadowed faces never drop below ~0.45× lit luma (sky.ts already specs this shadowStrength floor).

techniqueStack.name: Single-scattering aerial perspective (the 'air between you and the floor')
techniqueStack.what: Atmosphere — the depth cue that makes a 2km valley read as a real drone shot. The high crest sits clear; the river floor 700m below recedes into sun-tinted haze. Replaces the flat `mix(col,hazeColor,haze)` paint.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Orthographic top-down means the slant air column to a fragment ≈ const vertical drone-altitude column + a horizontal term scaled by (camAltitude - fragElev). Compute opticalDepth = exp(-(fragElev - minElev)/H_scale)*columnLen (Rayleigh-ish height falloff, H_scale~600m). transmittance=exp(-beta*opticalDepth); inscatter = inscatterColor*(1-transmittance) where inscatterColor is a blend of skyColor (away from sun) and sunColor (toward sun) weighted by a cheap HG phase on the view-to-sun azimuth (view is straight down, so phase keys off sunDir.z and a forward-scatter lobe near the terminator → warm haze hugging the sunlit slopes at golden hour). col = col*transmittance + inscatter. beta scales with weather (visibilityM 600-4000 maps to extinction).
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.3ms (a couple exp() + the existing heightAt already sampled). Folds into the relief pass, no extra draw.
techniqueStack.risk: Medium-legibility: too much extinction buries the floor read at dawn (contract #4). MITIGATION: cap inscatter alpha at a legibility floor (≤0.55 like the old fogStrengthMax), and key beta off the SACRED visibilityM so it can never exceed what the weather already declares. Physically the orthographic column approximation is a cheat but reads correct because the eye reads relative haze-by-altitude, which this nails.

techniqueStack.name: Raymarched valley fog volume with in-scatter (true volumetric, not a height-mix)
techniqueStack.what: Atmosphere — the Korengal dawn: fog pooled in the river draw, ridges poking out, the fog itself lit warm where the sun reaches it and cool in shadow. Upgrades the reused floor-field fog from `mix()` to a short volumetric integral.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Reuse the 128² local-floor min-field (atmosphere-model.ts) — fog top = localFloor + diurnalFog(hour). For the top-down ray (origin = drone alt, dir straight down to fragElev), march ~6-8 steps through the [fragElev, fogTop] overlap. At each step: density = smoothstep at the fog top edge × a slow 3D-ish fbm (the prelude fbm2 advected by wind for drift); accumulate transmittance (Beer-Lambert) and in-scatter = density*stepLen*(sunColor*sunI*sampleCastShadow(p) + skyColor*skyI). The cast-shadow sample per step is what makes the fog go dark under a ridge and bright in the open — the seed of god-rays. Composite fogColor (now an in-scatter accumulation, sun-tinted) over the lit ground.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.9ms when fog present (6-8 taps of height + cast-shadow per fragment, but ONLY runs where fragElev<fogTop — early-out covers most of a clear day at 0ms). iGPU fine.
techniqueStack.risk: Medium: 8-tap march at screen-res on SwiftShader is the heaviest per-frame item. MITIGATION: step count LODs with fog presence and zoom (2 steps strategic, 8 close); early-out `if(fragElev>fogTop) skip`; the cast-shadow texture is already resident (no rebake). Legibility: fog density clamped below the floor so the river draw is veiled, never opaque (contract #4).

techniqueStack.name: Volumetric god-rays / light shafts (THE shot)
techniqueStack.what: Atmosphere/FX — at low sun (blue/golden hour) the beam rakes between ridgelines and visible shafts fan across the fogged draws. This is the single image attempt-1 never attempted and the one that makes the skeptic gasp.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Two coupled mechanisms: (a) the fog raymarch above already produces shaft-shaped brightness because each step samples the cast-shadow map — where the ridge shadow has a gap, in-scatter spikes along the lit columns. (b) Add a screen-space radial-blur god-ray pass for the airborne haze ABOVE the terrain: render a 'light mask' (bright where cast-shadow=lit AND aerial-haze present, projected to the on-screen sun azimuth even though sun is geometrically below the horizon — we place a virtual sun-anchor along sunDir.xy off-screen), then 32-tap radial blur toward that anchor (Mitchell-style decay), additively composited and gated by `(1-sunUp)` so it ONLY appears at low sun and vanishes at noon (correct — no shafts at high sun). Strength × sunI × fogPresence so weather/night modulate it.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.7ms (half-res light mask + 24-32 tap radial blur at half-res, upsampled). Only active when sunAltDeg<~12°, so 0ms most of the day.
techniqueStack.risk: Highest visual-payoff / highest taste risk. Overdone = cheesy lens-flare game. MITIGATION: cap shaft intensity hard, tie it to fog presence (no fog → no shafts, physically honest), and key the virtual sun-anchor to the REAL sunDir.xy azimuth so shafts always rake from the true sun side (toward NE at dawn, NW at dusk on a north-up map). Determinism: anchor is from the sim clock, blur is screen-space, no wall-clock. If it reads gimmicky in review → cut the screen-space pass (b), keep the physically-true in-fog shafts (a) which are subtler and safer.

techniqueStack.name: Threshold bloom (highlights breathe)
techniqueStack.what: Post — sunlit snow crests, the river sun-glitter, and bright HESCO at golden hour get a soft halo. The unmistakable tell of HDR film vs flat paint.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: After the HDR terrain target: bright-pass (luma>1.0, soft knee) into a half-res RGBA16F, then a separable Gaussian (2 passes × ~9 taps) at half then quarter res for a wide soft bloom, upsample-add back into the HDR target BEFORE tonemap (so ACES rolls the bloomed highlights naturally). Bloom strength from sky.grade (a touch more at golden hour). Reads only the HDR buffer — no sim data.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.5ms (bright-pass + 2 blur passes at reduced res). iGPU negligible.
techniqueStack.risk: Low. Legibility: bloom is highlight-only and pre-tonemap so it can't wash mid-tones or the tactical layer (which is a separate 2D canvas on top, never touched). MITIGATION: knee at luma 1.0 keeps daytime mid-ground bloom-free.

techniqueStack.name: Real water shader for the river/fords (kill the baked blue stripe)
techniqueStack.what: Water — the river becomes a live reflective surface: Fresnel sky-mirror, animated normal ripples, a sun-glitter specular streak that blooms at low sun, depth-darkened channel. Currently a baked color + sine. Reads as the river you'd actually see from a drone.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Where landAt==River/Ford/Marsh (sampled via a landcover-id texture, see below): build a water normal from two scrolling fbm-derivative layers (wind-advected, so it drifts with the sim wind, freezes on pause). Fresnel F=mix(0.02,1,(1-N·V)^5) — but V is straight down (ortho) so Fresnel is near-grazing only at ripple slopes → glints. Reflected sky color = skyColor (cheap env). Sun specular = pow(max(0,reflect(-sunDir,waterN)·V), shininess)*sunColor*sunI → a bright streak that exceeds 1.0 and feeds bloom (the golden-hour sun-glitter). Channel depth from distance to centerX darkens the deep line. River is a tiny fraction of screen pixels so cost is trivial.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.2ms (gated to water fragments only, ~2-4% of pixels). iGPU negligible.
techniqueStack.risk: Low-medium. MITIGATION: needs a landcover-id texture resident (1 Uint8 512² R8, ~256KB — built once from terrain.land). Legibility: water stays recognizably the river-blue family; glitter capped so it never strobes (normals are spatial-hash + clock-advected, deterministic).

techniqueStack.name: Drifting cloud shadows with soft penumbra (aerial-footage motion)
techniqueStack.what: Atmosphere — big soft cloud shadows slide across the valley with the wind, dimming the sun beam, exactly like watching real drone footage. Reused from attempt-1 but upgraded with multi-octave shape + penumbra that softens with cloud altitude.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Procedural fbm of (world + cloudOffset)*cloudScale (cloudOffset integrated from sim wind by the reused advanceCloud()). Upgrade: 3-octave fbm for ragged edges + a second low-freq layer for cloud-mass coverage; penumbra via smoothstep width that widens with assumed cloud altitude (soft, not hard-edged). Dims ONLY the direct sun term (not ambient) → shadowed ground stays lit by sky-fill (legible). Per-weather density/coverage already tabled in atmosphere-model.ts.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.15ms (a few fbm octaves, folds into relief pass).
techniqueStack.risk: Low. Determinism: drift integrated from sim clock, freezes on pause (already proven in attempt-1). Legibility: dims beam only, floor held by ambient (contract #4).

techniqueStack.name: Cast-shadow march with refined penumbra (reuse + soften)
techniqueStack.what: Terrain — the multi-km ridge shadows at low sun (the marquee Korengal dawn). Reuse the exponential-stride 56-step march verbatim; refine the penumbra to widen with distance from the occluder so far shadows are soft and near ones crisp (physically correct umbra growth).
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Keep SHADOW_FRAG's exponential stride into a R8 (or R16F for soft) FBO, rebaked only on sun motion. Refinement: track the max-overshoot distance and widen the final smoothstep penumbra ∝ that distance/tanAlt (a far ridge casts a soft edge, a near rock a sharp one). Sampled by the relief pass, the fog raymarch, AND the god-ray mask — one shadow source, three consumers, no fork.
techniqueStack.costMs: Rebake ~1.2ms but amortized (only on sun move, ~once/game-minute at 1×); per-frame sample is 1 texture read.
techniqueStack.risk: Low — proven in attempt-1. MITIGATION: keep the 1.5m self-shadow lift to kill acne on 5m cells.

techniqueStack.name: Procedural detail materials + micro-normals at close zoom (real ground)
techniqueStack.what: Terrain/veg — at Close band (ppm>3) the ground resolves into actual surface: scree gets micro-relief self-shadow, scrub a soft sheen, snow sparkles, cropland shows furrow normals. Replaces attempt-1's single fbm 'grain' multiply. This is what makes Close zoom stop being a smeared bitmap.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: A landcover-id texture (the R8 from the water tech) selects a per-class detail routine, zoom-faded by `clamp((ppm-2)/2)`. Each synthesizes a DETAIL NORMAL (perturb the relief normal) + albedo modulation from world-anchored fbm/voronoi: scree=high-freq voronoi cell normals (self-shadowing rock); scrub=soft bumps + a forward-scatter sheen on N·H; snow=sparse high-freq specular glints (>1.0 → bloom); cropland=directional furrow sine along the contour. All world-space so it pans, never shimmers (spatial hash). The perturbed normal feeds the SAME lighting math, so detail is LIT correctly, not painted.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.4ms at Close (gated off when ppm<2 → 0ms strategic/operational). iGPU fine.
techniqueStack.risk: Medium-legibility: micro-normals must not fight the macro relief read. MITIGATION: detail-normal strength capped low and faded by zoom; never active at the bands where terrain-shape reading matters most (strategic/operational).

techniqueStack.name: Time-of-day color grade as real WB + tonemap input (not a fillRect wash)
techniqueStack.what: Post — the documentary-frame look: warm-balanced amber golden hour, cool desaturated scotopic night, neutral noon. Reuses sky.ts GRADE_KEYS but applies them as pre-tonemap white-balance + post-tonemap lift/gamma, NOT attempt-1's source-atop fillRect over a finished bitmap.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: In the final tonemap pass: input HDR *= whiteBalance (linear WB gain from sky.grade), apply ACES, then in display space apply saturation (luma-lerp) + shadow lift (sky.grade.lift on (1-luma)). Exposure already folded once (single-fold rule from sky.ts preserved). The 2D tactical layer above is NEVER graded (contract #2) — the grade lives entirely in the HDR terrain pass.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.1ms (folds into the tonemap pass, a few mults).
techniqueStack.risk: Low. MITIGATION: saturation floor at night so the valley desaturates but faction terrain cues don't go fully grey; the SACRED ungraded-symbology contract is structurally guaranteed because grade touches only the GL canvas, not the 2D one.

techniqueStack.name: Screen-space directional sprite relight (assets join the light)
techniqueStack.what: Asset — the unchanged flat-SVG buildings/HESCO/trees stop wearing baked noon shading at 19:00. A one-pass relight tints the sprite layer by SkyState so a B-hut is amber-lit from the west and cool-shadowed east at dusk, blooms a rim at golden hour.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Sprites are rasterized to a sprite-layer FBO (or the existing sprite atlas blit captured to a buffer). A screen-space pass applies SkyState: multiply by a directional tint (warm toward sun-azimuth half of each sprite via a cheap screen-gradient keyed to spriteShadow.dx/dy, cool away), add the sky.grade sprite-tint, and let bright edges feed the shared bloom. Uses sky.ts's existing `spriteTint` + `spriteShadow` (already computed, capped at 0.5 alpha for legibility). Keeps the tactical SYMBOLOGY layer separate and ungraded.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.3ms (one screen-space pass over the sprite layer).
techniqueStack.risk: Medium: must distinguish world-dressing sprites (relight) from tactical symbols (never touch) — the existing layer separation in WorldView already does this. MITIGATION: relight only the decoration/structure sprite pass; the sprite-tint alpha cap (0.5, already in sky.ts) guarantees faction accents survive deepest night (contract #2).

techniqueStack.name: Film finish: grain + vignette + subtle chromatic aberration
techniqueStack.what: Post — the final 5% that says 'graded documentary frame' not 'game render'. Fine sensor grain, a breath of corner vignette, a hair of lateral CA at the extreme corners.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: In the tonemap pass tail: vignette = smoothstep falloff on screen radius (very gentle, ~0.92 at corners); grain = a hashed dither scaled by a wall-clock-free per-frame seed — BUT for determinism in screenshots, seed grain from sim-clock fract so it's reproducible (or disable in the screenshot harness); CA = sample R/B channels at ±0.5px radial offset growing toward corners only. All sub-millisecond, all in the existing fullscreen pass.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.1ms (folds into tonemap pass).
techniqueStack.risk: Low. MITIGATION: CA and vignette kept extremely subtle (corner-only, the center where tactical reading happens is untouched — contract #4); grain amplitude low so it textures without obscuring. Grain is the only optionally-wall-clock element; gate it to sim-clock or off under the deterministic harness.

proposals.theOneHolyShitMoment: Dawn, Operational band, light fog (the exact frame attempt-1 shipped flat as `dawn-operational.png`). The sun sits at +4° altitude in the NE, geometrically just clearing the eastern ridge. The cast-shadow march throws a multi-kilometer cool-blue shadow across the entire valley floor — and where the ridgeline has a notch, a column of warm direct light spills through. In that lit column, the raymarched valley fog pooled in the river draw IGNITES: the fog raymarch samples the cast-shadow map per step, so the in-scatter spikes exactly along the lit columns and stays dark under the ridge — producing true, geometrically-anchored GOD-RAYS fanning down the draw, with the screen-space radial pass extending them up into the airborne haze toward the real NE sun-azimuth. The wet river surface throws a blooming gold sun-glitter streak down its length. Aerial perspective makes the far north end of the valley recede into warm haze-blue while the near crest stands clear and sharp. The whole frame resolves through ACES so the amber highlights roll off like film instead of clipping, threshold bloom haloes the lit fog and the glitter, and the warm-balanced golden-hour grade ties it together — and crisp white contours and tactical symbols sit perfectly welded on top, ungraded, because they're on the 2D canvas. A soldier looks at that and says 'that's a drone feed of the Korengal at first light,' and the same frame is still a readable tactical map. Attempt-1 rendered that scene as a flat painted hillshade with an orange fillRect. This renders it as light passing through air.
proposals.legibilityPlan: The legibility contract is enforced structurally, not by taste, at all four bands. (1) Contours/units/HUD/reticles live on the SEPARATE 2D canvas ABOVE the GL canvas — the entire cinematic pipeline runs in the GL pass and physically cannot touch them (contract #1, #2 guaranteed by architecture, not discipline). The bit-faithful heightAt/normalAt keeps contours welded to relief. (2) NOON ANTI-INVERSION (contract #3): the sun due-south on a north-up map is near-flat, so the `u_formLightNW` guard blends a fixed NW key into the diffuse ONLY near noon, keeping a form-light read; aerial perspective and fog auto-vanish at high sun (inscatter keyed to terminator, fog burns off by 10:00, god-rays gated by 1-sunUp), so noon is clean, flat-but-readable relief at every band. (3) FLOORS (contract #4): aerial-perspective inscatter capped ≤0.55, fog density capped below opaque, cloud shadows dim DIRECT light only while sky-fill holds the floor at ~0.45× lit luma, sprite-tint alpha hard-capped at 0.5 — no combination of weather+night can bury the read. (4) BAND-AWARE COST/DETAIL: micro-normals and the heavy fog raymarch step-count LOD UP with zoom (off at strategic, full at close), so strategic/operational stay shape-dominant relief maps and close zoom gets real surface — the band where each read matters. (5) The film finish (vignette/CA) is corner-only; the screen center where tactical reading happens is untouched. (6) DETERMINISM: every world-anchored phenomenon (shadows, fog, clouds, god-ray anchor, water normals) is driven by the sim clock + integrated wind, never wall-clock; only optional grain touches wall-clock and is gated to sim-clock/off under the screenshot harness. Engine stays React-free; all of this is in the render layer reading SkyState/AtmoState/Terrain.
phasePlan: P0 — HDR foundation + honest relighting. Reuse the recovered two-canvas skeleton, sky.ts, atmosphere-model.ts, heightAt/normalAt, and cast-shadow march verbatim. Strip topo.ts's bake to FLAT linear albedo (delete the baked NW-key shade, altitude tint, haze — they move to the shader). Render terrain into RGBA16F, recompute diffuse+sky-fill+moon lighting in linear radiance, resolve through ACES + WB/sat/lift grade in a final fullscreen pass. Build the landcover-id R8 texture. Gate: tsc/build/lint/smoke/balance green; visual-matrix screenshots at 4 bands × dawn/noon/dusk/night match the live sim clock; noon does NOT invert. This alone should already beat attempt-1 (real tonemap + computed light, not paint).

P1 — Atmosphere as light transport. Add single-scattering aerial perspective (column extinction + sun-tinted inscatter) and convert the floor-field fog from mix() to the 6-8 step raymarch with per-step cast-shadow in-scatter. Gate: dawn fog pools in the river draw and burns off by 10:00; far valley recedes into haze; legibility floors hold (inscatter ≤0.55, fog not opaque); cost honest on SwiftShader (early-out verified). Commit.

P2 — The god-rays + bloom. Threshold bloom (bright-pass + separable blur, pre-tonemap). Then the screen-space god-ray pass anchored to the real sun-azimuth, gated by (1-sunUp)×fogPresence. Tune intensity caps hard. Gate: the holy-shit dawn-operational frame; shafts vanish at noon; no strobe; reads as film not lens-flare. This is the riskiest-taste phase — review screenshots before committing, fall back to in-fog-shafts-only if the screen-space pass reads gimmicky.

P3 — Water + cloud-shadow polish. Real river water shader (Fresnel sky-mirror + animated normals + blooming sun-glitter, gated to water fragments via the id texture). Upgrade cloud shadows to multi-octave + altitude-soft penumbra. Gate: river reads as live water at all bands, glitter blooms at low sun, no shimmer (deterministic normals); cloud shadows drift with sim wind, freeze on pause.

P4 — Close-zoom detail materials. Per-landcover procedural detail normals + albedo (scree/scrub/snow/cropland), zoom-faded, feeding the same lighting. Gate: Close band resolves into real surface, micro-normals don't fight macro relief, off at strategic/operational. Commit.

P5 — Sprite relight + film finish. Screen-space directional relight of the world-dressing sprite layer from SkyState (tactical symbology untouched). Final grain/vignette/subtle CA in the tonemap tail, grain gated to sim-clock/off under harness. Gate: assets sit IN the light at every time-of-day; full 4-band × times × weathers matrix re-shot; all standing checks green; before/after screenshots recorded in docs/progress/; HTML report published to the archive.
proposals.riskiestBet: The screen-space god-ray pass (technique 5b) is the most likely thing to fail review or get cut — it is the single highest visual-payoff effect and also the one most prone to reading as a cheesy lens-flare game effect rather than documentary footage, and it requires faking an on-screen sun-anchor for a sun that is geometrically below the horizon at the exact low-sun times the shafts want to appear. SECONDARY risk: RGBA16F renderability under headless SwiftShader — if the half-float color attachment isn't renderable, the whole HDR foundation needs the RGBA8 packed-exposure fallback (probed at init). FALLBACK for the god-rays: the physically-true in-fog shafts (technique 5a — in-scatter spiking along lit columns in the fog raymarch) are subtler, geometrically honest, and survive on their own; if 5b reads gimmicky in P2 review, cut it entirely and keep 5a, losing the airborne-haze shaft extension but keeping the in-draw god-ray read that carries the holy-shit frame. FALLBACK for HDR: packed-exposure RGBA8 keeps the entire pipeline shape (tonemap, bloom, grade) at the cost of some highlight precision — acceptable, and the screenshot harness is the only consumer that strictly needs SwiftShader, so I'll probe-and-branch at init exactly as the recovered skeleton already branches for the 2D fallback.

proposals.northStar: THE LIVING VALLEY. Attempt-1 made the sun move over a corpse; this proposal makes the valley *breathe*. The thesis: photoreal aerial truth in a top-down COIN map does not come from a prettier static surface — it comes from MOTION and WATER, the two things a real drone feed has that a painted bitmap can never fake. A soldier who has watched Restrepo knows the Korengal river is not a blue stripe: it is a braided, sun-glinting, foam-flecked thread of moving water in the bottom of the draw, and the forests are not green felt but a dense, self-shadowing, wind-stirred canopy whose tops catch the low sun while the trunks sit in cold blue shade. We render the river as a true animated water *surface* — flow advected along the centerline, fresnel sky reflection, depth-tinted shallow-to-deep, whitewater foam blooming at fords and steep channel cells — and the vegetation as a procedural canopy *volume* with parallax, color variation, sun-tracked cast shadow and wind sway, never a flat sprite field. Then weather stops being a screen overlay and becomes a force acting ON that surface: rain darkens and wets the ground (raising specular), pools in the river draw, streaks the air; snow accumulates by slope and altitude into a real white field; dust lifts off dry ground on the wind; smoke from fires drifts and casts soft shadow. Everything world-anchored runs off the ONE master clock and the live SkyState — pause the sim and the water stills, the canopy freezes mid-sway, the rain stops in the air. The valley is alive because the simulation is alive, and you can read every bit of it. The bar: pause on the dawn river ford and the skeptic cannot tell it from a real UAS still.
proposals.whatMakesThis10x: Attempt-1's entire surface was `col = albedo * (0.34 + 0.95*shade)` — a hillshade multiply over a pre-painted bitmap, with a sine() "ripple" tint standing in for water and 2D screen-space particles floating over it all. The 10x leap is four concrete category changes, none of which attempt-1 had at all: (1) The river becomes a SECOND render pass with a real water BRDF — animated flow-advected normal map driving fresnel sky reflection + sun specular glint, depth-tinted body color (shallow gravel-teal to deep slate), and a foam field that blooms where the channel is steep (slope texture) or shallow (fords) and is ADVECTED downstream so it visibly moves. No game ships a top-down tactical map with shaded animated water; this is the marquee. (2) Vegetation stops being scattered flat SVGs and becomes a canopy material: a forest density field (terrain.conceal) drives a multi-octave canopy-noise lit as a 3D-ish lobe (NW-key crescent + cold SE shade baked from normals), with hue variation per clump and a real sun-tracked drop shadow that rakes the ground at golden hour, plus wind sway sampled from windVector(). (3) Weather becomes a STATE OF THE GROUND, not an overlay: a wetness accumulator and a snow-depth accumulator (both world-anchored, integrated off the sim clock) physically modify the terrain material — wet ground darkens and goes specular, puddles fill the river draw via the same local-floor field the fog uses, snow whitens by slope+altitude and fills shadow with cold bounce. (4) A real tonemap + bloom + AO post chain replaces the flat clamp, so sun glints on water and snow crests actually bloom and shaded draws get contact darkening. This is transformation: the surface is now made of materials that respond to light, water, and weather, not a filtered photograph of one.

techniqueStack.name: Flow-advected animated river surface (the centerpiece)
techniqueStack.what: WATER. The river/ford/marsh becomes a true water surface with a moving, normal-mapped skin instead of a dead blue ribbon. This is the single biggest departure from attempt-1's flat sine-ripple tint.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Bake once on the CPU (deterministic, from centerXAt + Land): a 512² RG8 'flow field' = unit downstream direction per river cell (derived from d(centerX)/dy and channel gradient), plus an R8 'river mask' (0 dry, distance-to-bank ramp for shoreline). In a dedicated water fragment pass (only fragments where mask>0, cheap), sample TWO scrolling octaves of a small tiling normal-map texture (128² RGBA8, generated once by curl-of-noise → tangent-space normals) offset by flowDir * (clockSeconds * speed), at two scales/phases, and blend (the standard Vlachos/'flowmap' trick) so the surface never visibly tiles or pulses. Perturb the water normal with this; compute fresnel = pow(1-dot(N,up),5) → mix(bodyColor, skyColor from SkyState hemisphere, fresnel); add Blinn specular glint toward sky.sunDir tinted sky.sunColor (this is what bloom catches at dawn). Depth tint: lerp shallow gravel-teal→deep slate by (bankDistance) so the channel reads 3D. All scroll math keyed to world.secondsOfDay → pause stills the water, time-warp speeds the current. Determinism preserved: no wall clock.
techniqueStack.costMs: SwiftShader ~1.0–1.8ms (extra fullscreen pass but masked: most fragments early-out on mask==0; two texture taps + math only on water). iGPU <0.3ms. Cache-resident: two 8-bit textures + the R32F height already loaded.
techniqueStack.risk: MED. Risk: glint too hot / strobes on SwiftShader low-precision → mitigate by clamping specular and folding it through the tonemap, and by deriving normals from a continuous flowmap (no per-frame randomness). Legibility: water stays inside river cells (mask-gated) so it can never bleed onto tactical ground; fresnel reflection is the SKY color (already legible), and at strategic zoom the river still reads as a coherent blue thread.

techniqueStack.name: Whitewater foam at fords, rocks & steep channel
techniqueStack.what: WATER. Foam blooms and ADVECTS downstream where water breaks: shallow gravel-bar fords (Land.Ford), steep channel cells (high terrain.slope along the river), and around cover-object boulders sitting in/near the channel. Turns 'cross at the ford' into a visible, churning, legible crossing.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Foam intensity = max(slopeBreak, fordMask, rockProximity), where slopeBreak = smoothstep on terrain.slope sampled along the channel and fordMask comes from the baked Land.Ford cells (dilated 1 cell). Animate by sampling a foam-noise octave scrolled along the same flowmap, with a sawtooth 'birth→fade' phase so foam appears at the break and dissolves downstream (advection illusion). Composite as additive near-white (#f3ecd6 per ART_BIBLE rim, never pure white) over the water BRDF, alpha = foam intensity. Ford foam doubles as the tactical 'this is a crossing' cue the old pale-teal tint gave, but alive.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.3ms (rides the water pass; one extra noise tap on already-water fragments). Negligible on iGPU.
techniqueStack.risk: LOW. Foam is gated to genuinely-broken water so it can't wash the map. Legibility WIN: fords become more obvious, not less.

techniqueStack.name: Procedural canopy material for forest/orchard (not flat sprites)
techniqueStack.what: VEGETATION. Forest, Orchard, Scrub render as a lit canopy VOLUME — domed, self-shadowing, color-varied — instead of attempt-1's flat green albedo + 2D SVG scatter. Reads as dense Hindu-Kush cedar/holly-oak from strategic down to close.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Drive off terrain.conceal (0..1 canopy density, already a Float32Array, upload as 512² R8). Where conceal>threshold, add a canopy layer in the terrain frag: multi-octave value-noise (the prelude fbm2, world-anchored) shaped into rounded lobes; light each lobe as a hemispherical blob — its own micro-normal from the noise gradient dotted with sky.sunDir gives the NW-lit-crescent / cold-SE-shade the ART_BIBLE specifies, tinted toward sky.sunColor on top and sky.skyColor (cool) underneath. Per-clump hue jitter (hash → ±10% within the locked forest palette #324c30..#527038) kills the felt-green flatness. The existing decoration.ts SVG sprites then layer on top ONLY at close zoom (lodAlpha) as hero detail — the canopy material carries strategic/operational/tactical, sprites carry close.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.6–1.0ms SwiftShader (a few extra fbm taps gated to canopy fragments). iGPU <0.2ms.
techniqueStack.risk: MED. Risk: canopy noise + relief shade fighting → keep canopy as a tinted modulation of albedo, not a replacement, so contours/relief still read through. Legibility: forest must stay clearly distinct from open ground at strategic zoom — enforce by keeping the dark base color dominant when zoomed out (canopy detail amplitude scales with ppm).

techniqueStack.name: Canopy & object cast shadows raked by the live sun
techniqueStack.what: VEGETATION/ASSET. The canopy and tall objects throw real soft drop-shadows onto the ground, sun-tracked, long at golden hour, short at noon — the depth cue that makes a forest read as having HEIGHT from above.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Two tiers. (a) Canopy: in the cast-shadow ray-march pass (reused SHADOW_FRAG), add a small height bump = conceal * canopyHeight(~7m) to heightAt so the existing exponential-stride march already throws canopy shadows for free into the same R8 visibility map. (b) Hero sprites: the existing sky.spriteShadow {dx,dy,lengthPerM,alpha} already gives 2D sprite shadows — keep, but feed canopy-consistent direction. The march is rebaked only on sun motion (existing throttle), so cost is amortized.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0 extra per frame (folds into the existing throttled shadow bake, which already runs ~1×/game-min). Bake itself unchanged in cost.
techniqueStack.risk: LOW. Reuses the proven, refuted-alternatives-survived shadow march. Only risk is canopy-height bump making ridge self-shadow noisier → clamp the bump and keep the 1.5m acne lift.

techniqueStack.name: Wind motion on canopy & grass (the valley stirs)
techniqueStack.what: MOTION. The canopy and open grass/scrub sway and shimmer along the live windVector() — gentle in calm air, whipping in a Rain/dust blow. The difference between a photograph and a feed.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Read world.windVector() → uniform u_wind (m/s, world frame). Offset the canopy-noise SAMPLE position by u_wind * sin(clockSeconds*freq + phaseFromWorldPos) * smallAmplitude — a per-clump phase from the spatial hash so the whole forest doesn't pulse in unison; amplitude ∝ |wind|. Grass/meadow gets a subtler high-freq shimmer in the same scheme. Keyed to world.secondsOfDay (NOT wall clock) so it freezes on pause and obeys time-warp — staying inside the determinism contract for world-anchored phenomena.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.1ms (one sin + offset on canopy fragments already being shaded).
techniqueStack.risk: LOW-MED. Risk: motion at close zoom could feel seasick → cap amplitude to a few pixels equivalent and gate to ppm so strategic view is still. Determinism: confirmed safe — clock-keyed, no RNG.

techniqueStack.name: Wetness accumulator → wet/specular ground in rain
techniqueStack.what: WEATHER. Rain doesn't just streak the air — the GROUND gets wet: darker, more saturated, and specular (a sheen that catches the overcast sky). A Rain day visibly soaks the valley over minutes and dries after.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: A scalar wetness W (0..1) integrated each frame off the sim clock from weather.precip (rises under Rain, falls when clear), stored in the store (the bridge) and passed as a uniform — world-anchored, deterministic, survives save via serialize/loadWorld (one float). In the terrain frag: darken albedo by mix(1, 0.7, W), boost saturation slightly, and add a low Blinn specular lobe toward the (cloud-dimmed) sky. Porosity per land class: rock/road go shiny fast, scree/dust slow, forest barely (canopy sheds). This is a MATERIAL response, the thing attempt-1 completely lacked.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.2ms (a few mults + one specular term, all fragments but trivial).
techniqueStack.risk: LOW. New persisted float must go in BOTH serialize() and loadWorld() (invariant). Legibility unaffected — it's a luminance/spec shift inside palette.

techniqueStack.name: Rain pooling in the draw via the valley-floor field
techniqueStack.what: WEATHER/WATER. Sustained rain pools water in low ground — the river draw widens, sheet-water films the floodplain — using the SAME local-floor min-field the fog pools from. Ties weather to terrain physically.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Reuse atmosphere-model's 128² local-floor R32F. Pooling height = wetness * rainPoolMax; where (localFloor + poolHeight - heightAt) > 0, treat the fragment as a thin water sheet → route it through the water BRDF (reflection + the wet specular) with a shallow depth tint. Pools advect nothing (still water) so just fresnel + sky reflection — cheap. Drains as wetness falls.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.2ms (gated to low-lying fragments during rain only).
techniqueStack.risk: LOW-MED. Risk: pooling on the wrong cells if min-field is coarse → clamp pool depth small so it only films true bottoms; gate hard to Rain. Legibility: pools are shallow and in dead ground, never on routes.

techniqueStack.name: Snow accumulation by slope + altitude (real white field)
techniqueStack.what: WEATHER. Snow ACCUMULATES into a coherent white surface that builds on flat high ground and sheds off steep faces and warm low floor — not attempt-1's falling-dot overlay. A Snow campaign day transforms the valley's albedo.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: A snow-depth accumulator S (0..1, world-anchored, integrated off clock from weather.label==Snow, melts when warmer/lower), one persisted float. Coverage mask = S * smoothstep(snowLine by altitude from heightAt) * (1 - slope*k) (flat catches, cliffs shed) * (1 - canopy*0.6) (forest holds less). Where covered: lerp albedo→snow white (#eaf0fa, in-palette cool), drop saturation, add a faint sparkle-spec and STRONG sky-ambient bounce (snow fills shadow with cold light — the signature high-altitude look). Permanent high-crest snow (existing bake's snowLine) becomes the S→1 limit.
techniqueStack.risk: LOW. Another persisted float (serialize+loadWorld). Legibility WIN: snow reveals terrain form beautifully (raking light on white); keep contours dark over it.

techniqueStack.name: Drifting cloud shadows + advected dust haze (aerial truth)
techniqueStack.what: WEATHER/ATMOSPHERE. Soft cloud shadows sweep the valley with the wind (already prototyped in attempt-1's atmo model — KEEP & strengthen), and on dry/windy Hazy days a warm dust haze lifts and advects, thickening downwind. The 'real drone feed' giveaway.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Reuse atmoState cloudOffset (integrated from windVector off the sim clock) + the fbm2 cloud-shadow term dimming the sun beam — already correct, just raise contrast and add a soft penumbra. Dust: a second low-freq fbm layer, warm-tinted (#9c8d63 dust palette), advected by cloudOffset, density ∝ weather.wind on Hazy, applied as a height-fogging haze that's THICKER near the ground (gate by altitude vs local-floor) so it reads as lifted dust, not uniform fog.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.4ms (rides existing atmo math).
techniqueStack.risk: LOW. Already proven world-anchored & deterministic. Within the legibility floor (capped opacity).

techniqueStack.name: Smoke/fire drift integration hook
techniqueStack.what: FX. Smoke from fires/blasts (the sim already emits Effect.kind smoke/blast) drifts on the same windVector and casts a soft moving shadow on the terrain, so a burning qalat or willy-pete screen actually shades the ground it drifts over — combat and weather share one wind.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: The 2D FX layer already draws smoke sprites; add a low-res (256²) R8 'smoke occlusion' accumulation texture the FX layer writes drifting blobs into (positions from Effect list, advected by windVector off the sim clock), sampled by the terrain frag to dim the sun beam exactly like cloud shadow. One shared texture, one extra tap.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.3ms (one texture tap + the FX layer's cheap blob splat).
techniqueStack.risk: MED. Risk: coupling render to the live Effect list cleanly across the layer line → the store (the one bridge) marshals Effect positions into the texture; engine stays React-free. Cut-safe: drop it and smoke stays 2D-only.

techniqueStack.name: Filmic tonemap + threshold bloom + screen-space AO post
techniqueStack.what: POST. A real post chain replaces attempt-1's flat `clamp(shade*0.94+0.02)`. ACES-ish tonemap gives the image photographic shoulder/toe; a cheap threshold bloom makes sun glints on WATER and SNOW crests glow (the dawn-on-the-river money shot); a depth/normal-derived AO darkens contact in draws and under canopy.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Render terrain+water+canopy to an RGBA8 (or RGBA16F if available, else 8-bit + careful exposure) FBO. Post pass: (1) AO = sample heightAt in a small kernel → openness estimate → darken creases/valley bottoms (cheap horizon-based AO on the height texture, no depth buffer needed). (2) Bright-pass threshold + a few-tap separable gaussian → additive bloom (small radius, gated so it only blooms speculars/snow, never the UI). (3) ACES filmic tonemap + the sky.grade WB/exposure/lift (reuse sky.ts grade()). Output to the canvas. UI/units/contours are on the SEPARATE 2D canvas above and are NEVER touched — the legibility contract holds by construction.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~1.5–2.5ms SwiftShader for AO+bloom+tonemap at viewport res (separable, few taps). iGPU <0.4ms. The one place to dial kernel taps down if SwiftShader budget is tight.
techniqueStack.risk: MED-HIGH (feasibility/cost). Risk: SwiftShader 8-bit FBO banding in bloom → use RGBA16F if exposed, else clamp bloom strength and dither. This is the most expensive item; AO+tonemap are the must-keeps, bloom is the first thing to scale down. Legibility safe: post touches only the GL terrain canvas, never symbology.

techniqueStack.name: River sun-glint sparkle & shoreline wet-darkening
techniqueStack.what: WATER detail. Close-zoom hero touches: a sparse animated specular sparkle on the moving water (sun dancing on ripples) and a darkened, slightly-specular wet margin on banks/fords where water meets land.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Sparkle: high-freq scrolled noise thresholded against the fresnel-specular term so glints pop only where the water normal faces the sun, scintillating as the flowmap moves (clock-keyed). Wet margin: along the river mask's shoreline ramp, darken adjacent ground albedo and lift its specular (capillary wetting) — sells the water as physically present, not pasted.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.2ms (rides the water pass, close-zoom gated).
techniqueStack.risk: LOW. Sparkle capped + tonemapped so it can't strobe. Gated by ppm so strategic view stays a calm thread.

techniqueStack.name: Depth-graded atmospheric perspective on the far valley walls
techniqueStack.what: ATMOSPHERE. The far ridgelines fade into cool haze with distance-from-camera-center, giving the orthographic top-down view a sense of vast scale and air — the Hindu-Kush depth that reads in every Restrepo wide shot.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Since it's orthographic, use ELEVATION + distance-from-river-floor as a depth proxy: high, far ridge faces get a stronger cool-haze mix (reuse u_hazeColor, sky.skyColor) than the floor. Strengthen attempt-1's altitude haze with a slope-facing-away term so back-lit far walls recede. Keyed to SkyState (warmer haze at golden hour).
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.1ms (a couple of mix() on the existing altitude grade).
techniqueStack.risk: LOW. Inside the locked palette; capped so crests never wash out (legibility item 3).

proposals.theOneHolyShitMoment: DAWN AT THE FORD. Camera at operational/tactical zoom on a river ford, clock at 05:20, weather Clear. The low sun (alt ~6°, due east-ish) rakes across the valley: the western canopy tops are lit gold while the draws sit in long cold-blue cast shadow thrown multi-kilometres by the ridge (the proven shadow march). The river is unmistakably MOVING — two scrolling normal octaves advect the surface downstream, the fresnel reflection shows the warm dawn sky, and a hard specular glint tracks the sun and BLOOMS through the post chain into a string of dancing highlights on the current. At the ford the water goes shallow and breaks into whitewater foam that you can watch being born at the gravel bar and dissolving downstream. The far ridge walls recede into cool dawn haze; a thin sheet of valley fog still pools in the draw, burning off where the sun has reached it. The canopy stirs — barely — on the morning anabatic wind. Then you hit pause: the water freezes mid-glint, the fog hangs, the canopy stops mid-sway. It is not an animation playing over a map; it is the simulation's own clock, stopped. The skeptic leans in, looks at the moving foam at the crossing and the bloomed glint on the current, and says 'holy shit, that's a real drone feed' — and then realizes the foam is exactly where the SOP says to cross. That single frame is produced by the water-BRDF + flowmap foam + cast-shadow march + bloom/tonemap + valley-fog + wind stack composing together, every element driven by the one master clock.
proposals.legibilityPlan: The legibility contract is enforced by CONSTRUCTION, not by restraint. (1) The two-canvas split is sacred: ALL of this lives on the lower WebGL2 canvas; contours, units, reticles, labels, HUD stay on the upper 2D canvas, crisp and ungraded — the post chain and every effect physically cannot touch symbology. Contours stay welded because the heightmap port (bit-faithful heightAt) is reused unchanged. (2) Every dynamic effect is LOD-gated by ppm and amplitude-capped: at STRATEGIC (≤0.35) water is a calm coherent blue thread, canopy is dark-mass-vs-open-ground, wind/sparkle/foam detail is near-zero, atmospheric haze gives readable relief — the satellite read. At OPERATIONAL terrain shape dominates (cast shadows + haze do the work). At TACTICAL structures/fords/canopy edges are sharp; foam makes crossings MORE obvious. At CLOSE the water surface, foam, wet margins and hero sprites resolve into real material. (3) Noon non-inversion is preserved by reusing attempt-1's `u_formLightNW` relief-guard blend (a fixed NW key folded in when the sun is due-south flat) — kept verbatim. (4) Weather floors: veil/haze/fog opacity capped exactly as today; wetness/snow are luminance shifts inside the locked palette, never occluders; fog burn-off keeps the floor readable. (5) Determinism: water scroll, foam advection, canopy sway, cloud/dust drift, wetness/snow accumulators, smoke drift are ALL integrated off world.secondsOfDay / the sim clock and survive save (new floats in serialize+loadWorld) — only screen-space precip streaks use wall clock, exactly as the contract permits. Engine stays React-free; the store remains the only bridge marshalling SkyState/AtmoState/wind/Effect data into uniforms.
phasePlan: Phase 0 — Re-floor on the reusable skeleton (game green, looks like attempt-1). Restore sky.ts, atmosphere-model.ts, terrain-gl.ts, shaders.ts and the WorldView two-canvas wiring from /tmp/itm-recover; confirm 2D fallback + context-loss; tsc/build/smoke/balance green; capture the 4-band×ToD baseline matrix as the 'before'. This is the known-good launchpad — NOT the deliverable.

Phase 1 — Kill the flat surface: add ACES tonemap + sky.grade + height-based AO in the terrain frag (replace clamp(shade*0.94+0.02)). Immediate photographic depth, zero new data. Screenshot the noon non-inversion gate to prove relief still reads. Commit.

Phase 2 — THE RIVER. CPU-bake the flow field (RG8) + river mask (R8) from centerXAt/Land/slope (deterministic, cached on Terrain like the albedo). Add the masked water pass: flowmap-advected normals, fresnel sky reflection, depth tint, sun glint. Clock-keyed scroll. Screenshot dawn ford close + strategic thread. Commit — this is the headline.
Phase 3 — Foam + wet margins + sparkle (rides the water pass). Foam at fords/steep-channel/rocks, advected; shoreline wet-darkening; close-zoom sparkle. Verify fords are MORE legible. Commit.
Phase 4 — Threshold bloom post pass (the glint now glows). Gate to speculars/snow; scale taps for SwiftShader budget; confirm UI canvas untouched. Commit.

Phase 5 — CANOPY material: conceal-driven lit canopy volume + per-clump hue jitter + canopy-height bump into the shadow march. Forest now has height from above. Screenshot forest-edge at all 4 bands (strategic distinctness gate). Commit.
Phase 6 — MOTION: wind sway on canopy/grass off windVector(), clock-keyed, amplitude+ppm capped. Verify pause freezes it. Commit.

Phase 7 — WEATHER as material: wetness accumulator (wet/specular ground + draw pooling) and snow accumulator (slope/altitude coverage + cold bounce). New persisted floats in serialize+loadWorld; smoke round-trips in scratch save test. Re-run full weather×ToD×band matrix. Commit.
