Phase 8 — Atmosphere polish: strengthen cloud-shadow penumbra, advected dust haze on windy Hazy, depth-graded ridge perspective. Optional smoke-occlusion hook if budget allows (cut-safe). Commit.

Phase 9 — Verify with fresh eyes: full 4-band × 6-ToD × 6-weather screenshot matrix vs the Phase-0 baseline + vs attempt-1's c5-final; per-frame cost honesty on SwiftShader-headless; skeptical legibility pass at each band; publish HTML report to the archive. tsc/build/lint/smoke/balance green.
proposals.riskiestBet: The post chain on SwiftShader (item 'Filmic tonemap + bloom + AO') is the riskiest bet for COST, and the animated water-BRDF is the riskiest for LOOK. Cost: the bloom pass adds a full extra FBO + separable blur at viewport resolution, and SwiftShader is software — if it blows the headless screenshot-harness budget (or 8-bit FBOs band visibly in the bloom), bloom is the first casualty. Fallback: tonemap + AO are cheap must-keeps that already deliver 80% of the photographic lift; bloom degrades gracefully to a tiny-radius, low-strength, glint-only effect or is dropped entirely without touching the rest of the stack (the water glint just won't 'glow', it'll still specular). Use RGBA16F FBO if SwiftShader exposes it, else dither the 8-bit. Look risk on water: low-precision SwiftShader normals could make the fresnel/specular strobe or the flowmap visibly tile. Mitigation is built into the technique — two-octave flowmap blend (no tiling), clock-keyed continuous scroll (no per-frame randomness), and specular clamped through the tonemap (no strobe); if the surface still reads wrong on software, the depth-tint + fresnel reflection alone (drop the high-freq sparkle) already beats the dead-blue ribbon decisively. The thing I'd deliberately NOT attempt in this pass: true screen-space reflections or refraction of the riverbed — fresnel sky-reflection + depth tint buys the photoreal read at a fraction of the cost, and real SSR on a top-down ortho software rasterizer is a cost trap with little legibility payoff.

proposals.northStar: The 164 flat SVG decals are the single biggest "icons-on-a-map" tell, and attempt-1's fix (strip the baked shadow, project a self-silhouette, hand-author 15 hero SVGs) was timid because it left every sprite a FLAT albedo lit by nothing. This proposal makes every asset a real LIT SURFACE under the same live sun that lights the terrain. The mechanism: a per-sprite GBuffer (albedo + tangent-space normal + height/displacement + baked AO + a material id) authored once and lit in a single instanced WebGL2 deferred pass that consumes the exact same `skyState()` SunDir/keyDir/grade the terrain shader reads. A guard tower then catches gold on its NW eave and throws a real multi-meter SE shadow at dawn that SWEEPS as the master clock advances; a qalat's mud walls self-shadow into their own courtyard; an MRAP reads as a metal volume with a specular hood-glint, not a sticker. On top of that GBuffer foundation, the hero built-places (COP HESCO ring, towers, B-huts, TOC, qalat clusters, vehicles, helo) are re-authored at 2-4x detail with baked AO and ground-contact darkening so the COP reads, from above, as a real fortified outpost dug into the dirt — and a village reads as stacked stone-and-timber qalats around a courtyard. The whole thing stays a legible tactical instrument because lighting is layered ON TOP of an always-present form read (the relief-inversion `formLightNW` guard extends to sprites), tactical symbology/units-in-combat stay on the ungraded 2D canvas, and every asset's footprint/anchor/registration is byte-identical to today.
proposals.whatMakesThis10x: Attempt-1 (and the art-seam judge plan) treated assets as flat albedo + a PROJECTED silhouette shadow + 15 hand-redrawn SVGs. That is parity-plus-a-drop-shadow. The 10x leap is three concrete, compounding moves: (1) DEFERRED-LIT SPRITES — every sprite ships a normal+height+AO GBuffer and is lit per-fragment by the live sun in a real shading pass, so it has self-shadowing, a directional rim, material specular, and a CAST shadow that tracks the clock — the asset stops being a decal and becomes a small lit model. Nothing in the current stack has any per-sprite lighting at all. (2) An OFFLINE BAKE PIPELINE that generates those GBuffers from authored sources (height-painted SVG layers / SDF extrusion), so 164 assets get form WITHOUT 164 hours of hand-illustration — the normal/AO are computed, not drawn. (3) PROCEDURAL BUILT-PLACE COMPOSITION — the COP and villages are not a scatter of independent icons but a composed scene: HESCO renders as one continuous extruded berm mesh with corner mitering and a sandbag parapet, buildings get baked contact-AO and dust aprons where they meet the ground, courtyards self-occlude. The result is the difference between "a map with building icons on it" and "a drone looking down at a built outpost."

techniqueStack.name: Per-sprite GBuffer atlas (albedo/normal/height/AO/material)
techniqueStack.what: ASSET stack. The foundation: every world sprite stops being one RGBA canvas and becomes 4 channels packed into texture atlases — albedo.rgb+coverage.a (RGBA8), normal.xy (RG8, z reconstructed) + height (B8) + AO (A8) packed into one RGBA8, and a small material-id atlas. This is the data that lets a sprite be lit instead of blitted.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Offline (build step) each authored asset is rasterized to a half-res master, then we derive: tangent-space normal from a height field (authored as a grayscale <g id='height'> layer in the SVG, or SDF-extruded from the silhouette — Sobel on height → normalize(vec3(-dx,-dy,1/strength))); AO from a screen-space horizon scan on the same height (8 directions, cheap, baked once); material id from a flat color key. Pack into a 4096² atlas (164 sprites at 256² master = fits with room). Atlas UV + footprint live in the existing AssetDef. Determinism: bake is build-time, output is a committed .ktx2/.png + generated manifest — no runtime RNG.
techniqueStack.costMs: 0 per frame (build-time bake, ~3-5 s once; atlas upload ~8 MB once at load). SwiftShader-safe: plain RGBA8 sampling.
techniqueStack.risk: Authoring effort to add height layers to 164 SVGs. Mitigation: SDF-extrude-from-silhouette gives every sprite a baseline bevel for FREE (puffed-up read), and we hand-author height layers only for the ~20 hero assets. Legibility risk nil — coverage.a preserves exact silhouette/registration.

techniqueStack.name: Instanced deferred sprite-lighting pass (the live sun on every asset)
techniqueStack.what: ASSET stack, the marquee. One WebGL2 instanced draw lights ALL visible world sprites in a single pass using the SAME skyState sunDir/sunColor/skyColor/grade the terrain reads. Replaces 164 individual ctx.drawImage blits with one GPU pass. This is what makes a tower 'lit and self-shadowed, not a flat decal.'
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Per-instance attributes: atlasRect, worldXY, footprintM, rot, heightScaleM, flags. Vertex builds a camera-space quad (reuse worldToScreen inverse from terrain VERT). Fragment: sample GBuffer, rotate the tangent-space normal by the sprite's rot into world frame (2D rotation of n.xy), then shade EXACTLY like terrain: key=max(0,dot(n,u_sunDir)) mixed with formLightNW guard, fill, hemisphere ambient from skyColor/groundColor, tint by sunColor, multiply by baked AO, add material specular (Blinn-Phong, exponent from material id — high for metal/glass, ~0 for cloth/mud). Output premultiplied so the existing 2D canvas composites it. Soldiers/vehicles are 'rotating' so they get the rotated-normal path; static buildings can pre-bake into world frame.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.6-1.2 ms for a few hundred sprites on SwiftShader (one instanced draw, GBuffer is cache-resident). Far cheaper than 164 CPU blits + the per-sprite shadow blits attempt-1 proposed.
techniqueStack.risk: Normal rotation must be in WORLD axes AFTER rot or rotating soldiers get lighting that spins with them (the exact bug the art-seam judge caught with HESCO). Mitigation: rotate n.xy by rot in the fragment, verified by a turntable screenshot probe. Legibility: lighting only MODULATES a form that's always present; AO floor keeps shaded faces readable.

techniqueStack.name: Sprite cast shadows via the terrain shadow FBO + per-sprite height
techniqueStack.what: FX/ASSET. Real cast shadows that track the master clock — a guard tower's shadow rakes across the HESCO and floor at dawn, swings through noon, lengthens at dusk. Not attempt-1's projected silhouette: a height-aware drop that grounds the object on the actual relief.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Two tiers. Tier 1 (cheap, all sprites): in the sprite fragment, project a soft contact-shadow ellipse stretched along sky.spriteShadow.{dx,dy,lengthPerM} scaled by heightScaleM — drawn as a pre-pass into the same deferred buffer under the sprites. Tier 2 (hero structures only): stamp the tall sprites' heights into a low-res 'object height' contribution to the existing 1024² shadow-march FBO so towers/qalats occlude SUN on neighboring sprites and terrain (one extra additive write during the sun-motion rebake, not per-frame). Length/azimuth come straight from skyState — zero new sun model.
techniqueStack.costMs: Tier 1 ~0.3 ms (folded into the deferred pass). Tier 2 ~0 per frame (only on sun-motion rebake, ≤4 Hz, same cadence as terrain shadows).
techniqueStack.risk: Tier 2 height injection could make a tall qalat shadow read as terrain in a paused still. Mitigation: cap object-shadow darkness below ridge-shadow darkness and keep it warm-tinted; cut Tier 2 first if it muddies the read (Tier 1 alone already beats attempt-1).

techniqueStack.name: Re-authored HESCO as a continuous extruded berm (not a dotted ring)
techniqueStack.what: STRUCTURE, highest COP payoff. The HESCO perimeter is currently a ring of identical rotated segment decals (reads as dots). Re-author as ONE swept wall: a continuous gabion berm with a sandbag parapet, mitered corners, a real gate cut, lit and self-shadowing as a unit.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Generate the ring as an instanced extruded strip from cop.fightingPositions/perimeter geometry: a triangle ribbon with a height profile (berm + parapet), gabion-cell normal/AO from a tiling material, the inner face in self-shadow. The wall is a single GBuffer-fed mesh in the deferred pass, so the whole ring lights coherently (NW arc bright, SE arc shadowed) instead of 60 decals each baking the same NW key. Gate is a geometry break + the existing ecp-gate hero asset.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.2 ms (one instanced strip, ~200 segments).
techniqueStack.risk: Must follow the exact perimeter the sim uses or the wall floats off the wire. Mitigation: drive it from cop layout geometry (radius/center/gate) which the renderer already reads; verify with the 02-cop-tactical screenshot.

techniqueStack.name: Hero structure re-author at 2-4x with baked AO + ground-contact
techniqueStack.what: STRUCTURE. TOC, B-huts/barracks, guard tower, DFAC, armory, qalat, mosque, vehicles, helo re-authored with real volume: roof material variation, sandbag courses, antennas/dishes as height geometry, and a baked ambient-occlusion + a dust/contact apron that darkens where the wall meets dirt.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Author each hero as layered SVG: an albedo layer + a height layer (roof higher than walls, parapet higher than roof). The bake pipeline (technique 1) turns height into normal+AO automatically, so the 'extruded box' look becomes genuine per-fragment shading lit by the live sun — the fake 2.5D bevel is replaced by real bevel lighting. Contact-AO is a darkening ring baked into the AO channel around the footprint base; a procedural dust apron (noise * landColor) is composited at the sprite base in the deferred pass.
techniqueStack.costMs: Folded into the deferred pass (no extra cost); bake cost is build-time.
techniqueStack.risk: Hand-authoring ~20 heroes is real work. Mitigation: prioritize by instance count (HESCO done separately, then B-hut/barracks since the COP has many, then tower/TOC as silhouette landmarks); non-hero assets ride the free SDF-extrude baseline.

techniqueStack.name: Vehicle & helo as lit metal volumes with specular
techniqueStack.what: ASSET. MRAP/HMMWV/UH-60/CH-47 get real body volume (rounded hull normals), a metal/glass material id, and a moving specular highlight that slides as the sun or the vehicle's heading changes — the strongest 'this is a real object' cue for the eye.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Height-painted hull → smooth normals via the bake. Material id flags metal (specular exponent ~40, mild Fresnel rim) and glass (windshield highlight). In the deferred fragment, Blinn-Phong spec = sunColor * pow(max(0,dot(n,halfDir)),exp) * sunIntensity, gated by a specMask in the material atlas so only painted-metal texels glint. Rotor disk on the helo is a separate low-alpha animated ring (wall-clock, screen-space — exempt like precip).
techniqueStack.costMs: Negligible (a few ALU in the shared deferred pass).
techniqueStack.risk: Specular on a top-down ortho map can read as a tech-demo glint. Mitigation: keep exponent modest, gate by material mask, cap intensity; this is the first flourish cut if a screenshot looks game-y.

techniqueStack.name: Soldier kit/pose readability in the GBuffer
techniqueStack.what: ASSET. Soldiers get a normal/AO so the helmet domes, shoulders/ruck read as raised volume catching the key light, and role-kit (SAW barrel, RTO antenna, medic bag) reads by silhouette+material rather than by a flat color blob.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Author soldier height as a top-down relief (helmet highest, shoulders/ruck mid, ground low). Rotating path lights the helmet dome consistently from any heading because the normal is rotated into world frame. Faction accent stays an UNLIT emissive channel (US-blue IR flag, ANA teal) so it survives night/grade — accents are legibility, not lighting.
techniqueStack.costMs: In the shared pass.
techniqueStack.risk: At <8 px (operational zoom) the lit detail is sub-pixel; mitigation is the existing LOD crossfade to a clean NATO symbol — lighting only matters in the tactical/close bands where soldiers are big enough to resolve.

techniqueStack.name: Live-sun terrain shader rebuilt as real materials (not albedo*shade)
techniqueStack.what: TERRAIN. Replace attempt-1's `col = albedo*(0.34+0.95*shade)` with a per-landcover MATERIAL model: each of the 26 Land classes carries roughness/spec/height-detail so rock glints hard and dusty crop is matte, lit by the same skyState. Keeps contours welded (same heightmap port).
techniqueStack.glslApproach: A 26-row material LUT (1D texture) keyed by a land-class texture (Uint8 → R8). Per-fragment: normal from heightmap (reuse the bit-faithful port) PERTURBED by per-class detail-normal (FBM-derived, scaled by ppm so it sharpens at close zoom), Blinn-Phong with class roughness, hemisphere ambient × class AO. River class gets a real animated normal-mapped water material (see next).
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.4 ms added to the existing terrain pass (a few taps + LUT).
techniqueStack.risk: Could over-texture and hurt the map read at strategic zoom. Mitigation: detail-normal amplitude ramps to ~0 below tactical ppm (LUT-gated), so the strategic band stays a clean relief.

techniqueStack.name: Real animated water material for the river/fords
techniqueStack.what: WATER. The river is currently a flat blue-ish landcover stripe with a sine ripple in the bake. Make it a true water surface: normal-mapped ripples advecting downstream, a sky-reflection tint, and a sun glint that tracks skyState — reads as flowing water from above.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: River mask from the land-class texture. Two scrolling FBM normal layers advected along the channel direction (centerX gradient gives flow dir) on the sim clock (deterministic, pause-safe). Shade = mix(waterDeepColor, skyColor reflection, fresnel(n,viewUp)) + sun glint pow(dot(n,half),highExp)*sunIntensity. Fords get a shallower, brighter, more transparent variant showing the gravel bar through.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.2 ms (only river texels do the extra work; masked early-out).
techniqueStack.risk: Glint could strobe at time-warp. Mitigation: advection is clock-driven and low-pass; glint exponent bounded; cut glint, keep ripples if it shimmers.

techniqueStack.name: Vegetation as lit canopy clumps with parallax, not flat dots
techniqueStack.what: VEG. The decoration scatter (trees/scrub/rocks) currently blits flat sprites. Give them GBuffer normals so a cedar canopy has a lit NW dome and shaded SE underside, and a subtle height-parallax so dense forest reads as a textured canopy from above rather than a field of identical stamps.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Decoration instances flow through the SAME deferred sprite pass with a canopy material (soft normal dome, high AO in the clump interior). Per-instance hue/scale jitter from the existing stable-hash (deterministic). Optional cheap parallax: offset the canopy albedo lookup by height*viewVec (view is straight down on ortho, so this is mostly a self-shadow term — keep it as AO darkening in the clump).
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.3 ms folded into the deferred pass for the visible scatter (instanced).
techniqueStack.risk: 1800-sprite cap at close forest could be heavy on SwiftShader. Mitigation: instancing makes this ONE draw vs 1800 blits — strictly cheaper than today; LOD-cull tiny instances.

techniqueStack.name: Filmic tonemap + restrained bloom on the world layer only
techniqueStack.what: POST. A real ACES-ish tonemap and a tight bloom on emissives (muzzle flashes, COP lights, sun glints) give the whole frame the photographic contrast of drone footage instead of flat sRGB — applied to the WORLD canvas, never to tactical ink.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Render terrain+sprites into an HDR-ish RGBA8 (or RGBA16F if available; fall back to RGBA8 with a pre-exposure on SwiftShader). Final fullscreen pass: bright-pass threshold → 2-tap separable blur at quarter res → add → ACES filmic curve → grade (exposure/WB/sat/lift from skyState). Tactical symbology/units-in-combat are drawn on the SEPARATE 2D canvas ABOVE this, untouched.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.5-0.9 ms (quarter-res blur + one fullscreen tonemap) on SwiftShader.
techniqueStack.risk: Bloom can wash the map at night if over-applied. Mitigation: bloom gated to emissive mask only; tonemap preserves the legibility floor (shadow detail never crushed below the contract); RGBA16F absent → pre-exposure path keeps it cheap.

techniqueStack.name: Contact/aerial AO between sprites and terrain (grounding)
techniqueStack.what: STRUCTURE/ASSET. A dark soft halo where any raised object meets the ground, so buildings/vehicles/HESCO sit IN the dirt rather than float ON it — the single cue that most separates 'composed scene' from 'pasted stickers.'
techniqueStack.glslApproach: In the deferred pass, accumulate a low-res 'occluder presence' buffer (object footprints splatted), then darken terrain ambient where presence is high near a footprint edge (a cheap SSAO-lite read of the presence buffer). Combined with the baked per-sprite contact-AO ring (technique 5) for the close read.
techniqueStack.costMs: ~0.3 ms (one low-res splat + one read).
techniqueStack.risk: Could double-darken with the baked contact ring. Mitigation: the screen-space term handles object-to-object/object-to-terrain; the baked ring handles the sprite's own base — tuned so they sum to one believable apron, verified at the COP screenshot.

techniqueStack.name: Strategic-band fallback to clean relief + symbols (legibility gate)
techniqueStack.what: LEGIBILITY. At ppm ≤ 0.35 all the material/specular/sprite-lighting detail crossfades OUT to the clean shaded relief + NATO symbols, so pulling out always yields a readable chart, never a noisy photo.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: A single u_detailGain uniform driven by ppm gates: detail-normals, specular, sprite GBuffer detail, bloom strength all multiply by it. Sprites crossfade to the existing screen-fixed symbol assets via lodAlpha (unchanged). This is a contract, not an effect — it's the guardrail that lets everything else 'go wild.'
techniqueStack.costMs: 0 (it REDUCES work when zoomed out).
techniqueStack.risk: None — it strictly protects the read. The risk would be forgetting it; mitigation is making detailGain a single audited uniform every technique multiplies through.

techniqueStack.name: 2D fallback parity (no-WebGL path keeps the game alive)
techniqueStack.what: ROBUSTNESS. When WebGL2/SwiftShader is unavailable or context is lost, the renderer falls back to the current flat-blit sprite path so the game never goes dark — same branch attempt-1 reserved.
techniqueStack.glslApproach: Keep the existing sprites.ts drawWorldSprite blit path as the fallback. The deferred path and the blit path share the same AssetDef/anchor/footprint, so a single `ok` flag selects between them at one branch (mirrors TerrainGL.ok). Albedo channel of the GBuffer IS the old flat sprite, so the fallback is literally today's look.
techniqueStack.costMs: N/A (only active when GPU path is down).
techniqueStack.risk: Drift between the two paths. Mitigation: the fallback consumes the same albedo atlas, so it can't visually diverge beyond 'no live lighting' — which is the accepted degraded mode.

proposals.theOneHolyShitMoment: Dawn over the COP, time-warped. The camera sits at tactical zoom on the outpost. As the master clock runs at 8x, the sun lifts off the east ridge and you watch the guard tower throw a long, hard SE shadow that rakes ACROSS the HESCO berm and out over the gravel — and that shadow SWINGS and SHORTENS in real time as the sun climbs, because it's driven by the same skyState the terrain shadow march uses. Simultaneously: the HESCO ring lights as one continuous berm (its NW arc catching warm gold, its SE arc dropping into self-shadow), the B-hut roofs catch a rim highlight on their NW eaves while their sandbagged SE walls go dark, a parked MRAP throws a sun glint off its hood that slides as the light moves, the qalat in the village across the river self-shadows into its own courtyard, and every soldier's helmet is a little lit dome casting a contact shadow on the dirt. The skeptic who watched Restrepo sees the exact thing they remember — the outpost waking up as the light comes over the wall — and says 'holy shit, an AI built this.' It works because ONE sun (skyState) drives terrain relief, terrain cast shadows, sprite lighting, sprite cast shadows, water glint, and the grade — so the whole frame moves as one coherent lit world instead of a hillshade with stickers and a filter.
proposals.legibilityPlan: The read is protected by construction at all four bands. STRATEGIC (≤0.35): u_detailGain → 0 crossfades out specular/detail-normals/sprite-lighting/bloom; sprites become the existing screen-fixed NATO symbols via the untouched lodAlpha path; you get a clean shaded relief + symbols chart. OPERATIONAL (0.35-1.2): terrain shape and the lit HESCO ring/building footprints dominate; sprite lighting is present but coarse; contours stay welded to relief because the heightmap port is unchanged. TACTICAL (1.2-3): the full lit diorama — structures, vehicles, soldiers all lit and self-shadowed — but units-in-combat, orders, fire reticles, threat crescents, labels and HUD are all drawn on the SEPARATE 2D canvas ABOVE the world layer and are NEVER graded, lit, bloomed, or fogged (the layer line is the legibility line). CLOSE (>3): material/detail resolves to real surface; faction accents are an UNLIT emissive channel so they survive deepest night and any grade. Cross-band invariants: (1) lighting only MODULATES a form that's always present — the formLightNW guard extends from terrain to sprites so noon (south sun, flat) never inverts or flattens the read; (2) an AO/ambient floor guarantees shaded faces never crush below the contract's legibility floor; (3) fog/weather fade scenery but floor symbology per the recovered per-class constants; (4) determinism holds — GBuffers and shadow geometry are pure functions of (clock, weather, terrain seed); only screen-space precip and the helo rotor disk use wall clock.
phasePlan: Phase 0 — Lighting bus: wire skyState() into the render loop as the single light source and add the instanced deferred SPRITE pass that lights existing albedo with a flat normal (n=up) only. Game green: sprites look identical to today (flat) but now go through the GPU pass and pick up the time-of-day grade. Proves the pass + the 2D-fallback branch with zero look change.

Phase 1 — Bake pipeline: extend build-asset-manifest.mjs to emit the GBuffer atlas (albedo+normal+height+AO+material). Baseline every asset with FREE SDF-extrude-from-silhouette so all 164 get a baseline bevel. Game green: sprites now catch the live sun with a generic puffed normal — first visible 'these have form' moment, no hand-art yet.

Phase 2 — Sprite cast shadows (Tier 1): contact-shadow ellipses stretched along skyState.spriteShadow. Game green: every grounded object is grounded and the shadows track the clock. Screenshot the dawn COP at the 4 bands.

Phase 3 — HESCO continuous berm + hero re-author wave 1 (B-hut/barracks, tower, TOC): author height layers, regenerate GBuffer. Game green: the COP reads as a real fortified place from above. This is the headline deliverable; verify against 02-cop-tactical.png.
Phase 4 — Terrain materials + water: per-class material LUT, detail-normals, animated river. Game green: ground reads as real surface at close zoom, river flows. Noon squint-test at all bands.

Phase 5 — Vehicles/helo specular, soldier kit GBuffer, contact AO, hero wave 2 (qalat/mosque/DFAC/armory). Game green: vehicles read as metal volumes, soldiers' kit reads, villages read as built places.

Phase 6 — Filmic tonemap + restrained bloom + Tier-2 object shadows in the FBO. Game green: the photographic 'drone footage' contrast lands. Full matrix: 4 bands × times-of-day × weathers, plus the dawn time-warp money shot. Each phase is a commit; standing checks (tsc/build/lint/smoke/balance) green at every one.
proposals.riskiestBet: The riskiest bet is the OFFLINE GBUFFER BAKE producing convincing normals/AO for the existing 164 assets without 164 hours of hand-illustration. If SDF-extrude-from-silhouette yields mushy, samey 'puffed-pillow' lighting on the non-hero assets, the cheap-volume promise collapses and the only thing that looks good is the ~20 hand-authored heroes. Fallback, in order: (1) hand-author height layers only for the high-instance/high-visibility assets (HESCO already separate, then B-hut, tower, MRAP, qalat, soldier, cedar) — these are 80% of the on-screen pixels at tactical zoom, so even if the long tail stays nearly flat the scene reads as transformed; (2) for the long tail, lean on cast-shadow grounding (Tier 1) + contact AO, which sell 'real object' without needing rich surface normals; (3) if even that underwhelms, the whole deferred pass degrades GRACEFULLY to the 2D-fallback flat blit (it shares the albedo atlas), so the worst case is 'today's look plus a coherent grade,' never a broken renderer. Secondary risk: the relief-inversion/legibility guard fighting the cinematic ambition at noon — mitigated by making formLightNW and detailGain audited single-uniform contracts that the noon-squint screenshot gate must pass before any phase merges.

bestGrafts: Material-ID + control-texture data spine (photoreal-drone): upload u_landId R8UI + u_control RGBA8 + a small surfaceState texture so the fragment RECOMPOSES the surface from the sim's own arrays instead of reading a pre-painted bitmap. This is the architectural move that lets ANY of the proposals stop being 'the old map with a filter.' It is the prerequisite the close band needs and the cheapest thing to verify (texelFetch==land[i] parity test).

World-scale per-landcover PBR material atlas + per-material detail-normal raking (photoreal-drone, also in cinematic/asset). This is the single technique that fixes attempt-1's actual worst frame (noon-close / dawn-close): the ground resolving into scree grains / furrow rows / canopy lobes instead of upscaling into a smear. Deterministic CPU bake from FBM+worley keeps the seed contract and needs no asset pipeline.

Flow-advected animated river surface keyed on Land.River/Ford/Marsh with two-octave flowmap normals + fresnel sky reflect + sun-tracked glint (living-valley's centerpiece, echoed in all four). The dead blue stripe is a tell in EVERY reference frame I looked at; this is high realism-per-effort (water is a tiny fraction of pixels, masked early-out) and it is the one element that most reads as 'a live drone feed' rather than a still.

Whitewater foam born-at-break / advecting-downstream at fords (living-valley). Rare graft that IMPROVES legibility instead of risking it — it makes 'cross at the ford' more obvious while selling moving water. Tie it to Land.Ford + channel slope.

HESCO re-authored as ONE continuous extruded berm with mitered corners + sandbag parapet + a real gate cut (asset-fidelity). The dotted-segment ring is the loudest 'icons on a map' artifact in the COP at tactical/close zoom in every reference image. A continuous self-shadowing berm is the highest single-asset payoff in the whole campaign and cheap (~0.2ms, one instanced strip).

Sprite cast shadows + contact-AO grounding driven by the SAME skyState the terrain uses (asset-fidelity Tier 1). Even without rich per-sprite normals, a tower throwing a real SE shadow that sweeps with the clock and a dust apron where wall meets dirt is what stops buildings floating ON the map and seats them IN it — the seam a photoreal ground over flat stickers would otherwise create.

Baked horizon-angle AO field (photoreal-drone HBAO-lite) reusing the existing shadow-march, multiplying the AMBIENT (not direct) term. Contact darkening in draw bottoms, cliff bases, terrace insides, and around buildings is in every real orthophoto and attempt-1 faked it with one n.z term.

Snow accumulation by altitude x aspect x slope as a real white field that reveals form under raking light (living-valley / photoreal-drone), as opposed to attempt-1's painted cap or falling-dot overlay. Reads as a real Hindu Kush spring and is a deterministic clock function. Keep it SLOW (campaign-scale), never a strobe.

Aerial perspective driven by altitude (all four, cleanest in cinematic-film's single-scattering form): the far valley wall recedes into sun-tinted haze while the near crest stays sharp — the Hindu Kush depth in every Restrepo wide shot. Keep it capped below the legibility floor (reuse the old fogStrengthMax<=0.55).

ACES filmic tonemap + the existing sky.ts grade applied as real WB/lift, replacing attempt-1's raw clamped linear write (all four). This is the cheap, low-risk move that turns flat sRGB paint into the highlight-rolloff of a sensor — worth doing even if the full HDR float-target pipeline is cut.

detailGain / detail-strength as a SINGLE audited ppm-gated uniform that every wild effect multiplies through (asset-fidelity makes this explicit). Turns the legibility floor from per-effect discipline into one guardrail — the right way to let the GL layer 'go wild' safely.
legibilityTraps: The two-canvas firewall (HUD/contours/units/reticles on the ungraded 2D layer above GL) is necessary but NOT sufficient, and all four lean on it as if it were. It protects SYMBOLOGY, but the WORLD-DRESSING read (is that a ridge or a draw? is that forest or open ground? where is the ford?) lives entirely in the GL layer and can absolutely be buried by over-textured materials, hot speculars, or fog. Every proposal must prove the WORLD read at all 4 bands, not just point at the firewall.

Detail-normal raking is sold as the photoreal trigger but it is the legibility trap at NOON. With the sun due-south and near-vertical (the brief's contract #3), NdotL is near-uniform across micro-facets, so over-strong normals either flatten to 'painted' OR fight the macro form-light and read as NOISE on what should be a clean relief chart. photoreal-drone names this as its riskiest bet honestly; the others underweight it. Mitigation must be numeric (formLightNW guard + detailStrength scales with sun rake-angle), not by eye.

Snow + heavy material detail on the CRESTS can bury the ridgeline silhouettes the player reads for LOS. The valley-IS-the-enemy: ridge form is gameplay-critical. Snow coverage must respect AO/relief and cap below the LOS ridgelines; over-textured rock must ramp detail to ~0 at strategic/operational where ridge SHAPE is the read.

cinematic-film's screen-space god-rays are an active legibility AND art-direction trap: a 32-tap radial blur toward a faked off-screen sun-anchor veils the airborne haze across the screen at exactly the low-sun times the player is reading long shadows. It can wash the operational read and reads as a video-game lens flare, the opposite of a sober ISR feed. The proposer flags it as cuttable, but it is the marquee of their holy-shit frame — cutting it guts their differentiator.

living-valley's canopy/grass WIND SWAY risks motion-sickness and, worse, a 'forest is shimmering' read that competes with combat motion for the eye on a tactical instrument. Amplitude+ppm capping is named but the failure mode (the whole map subtly crawling) directly fights the 'sober chart' half of the bar. Motion should be reserved for water (which legibly SHOULD move) and near-zero on vegetation.

Wet-ground sheen and water glint can over-specular into glare that strobes at time-warp on low-precision SwiftShader, blowing out the tactical read over the exact river crossing the player is planning. All four name clamping; the trap is that SwiftShader's 8-bit precision makes the clamp threshold finicky and a single hot frame in a screenshot is a fail.

asset-fidelity's specular metal on vehicles and 'sparkle' on snow/water are the easiest place for a tech-demo tell to creep in on a top-down ortho map — a sliding hood-glint with no parallax can look like a game prop, not an ISR object. Gate hard by material mask and cut first.

ACES + linear-space relighting shifts overall brightness vs the byte-faithful baseline; if the noon-clear mid-gray luma calibration gate is skipped, the relief can invert or wash at the exact band the contract forbids. Only photoreal-drone and cinematic-film name this calibration gate explicitly.
feasibilityTraps: RGBA16F HDR RENDER TARGET under headless SwiftShader is the load-bearing, UNVERIFIED assumption for cinematic-film (it makes 'rendering moves to linear HDR' its #1 differentiator) and is used by photoreal-drone/living-valley/asset-fidelity for bloom. The PROVEN recovered stack renders the terrain pass directly to the RGBA8 default framebuffer and only uses an R8 FBO for shadows + R32F for height (probing only OES_texture_float_linear). No float color attachment is in the working baseline. The RGBA8 packed-exposure fallback (named by photoreal/cinematic) is honest but degrades highlight range exactly where golden-hour and bloom live. This must be probe-and-branched at init before any phase depends on it.

cinematic-film's heaviest per-frame item is the 6-8 step valley-fog RAYMARCH with a per-step cast-shadow tap, at screen resolution, on a SOFTWARE rasterizer (SwiftShader) that the screenshot harness REQUIRES. ~0.9ms is claimed for iGPU; SwiftShader is software and the harness is the only consumer that strictly needs it. Early-out on clear days helps but the dawn-fog holy-shit frame is precisely when the march runs full. This is the most likely budget blowout in the set.

asset-fidelity's whole '10x without 164 hours of hand-art' promise rests on SDF-extrude-from-silhouette producing convincing normals/AO for the long tail of 164 assets. The proposer flags this honestly: if it yields 'puffed-pillow' samey lighting, only the ~20 hand-authored heroes look good and the rest read as inflated stickers — a NEW tech-demo tell. The graceful-degrade-to-flat-blit fallback means worst case is 'today plus a grade,' which is exactly attempt-1's failure mode.

Per-sprite normal rotation must happen in WORLD axes AFTER the sprite's heading rotation, or rotating soldiers/vehicles get lighting that spins with them (the exact bug the original art-director judge caught). asset-fidelity names it and prescribes a turntable probe — but it is a real correctness trap that the deferred-sprite pass lives or dies on.

living-valley and asset-fidelity add NEW PERSISTED FLOATS (wetness, snow-depth) to the save. The invariant is that new persisted state goes in BOTH serialize() AND loadWorld() with a migration. Easy to half-do; a same-seed divergence from a missed field IS the determinism bug the contract forbids.

The material atlas (photoreal-drone, 2048-square RGBA8 + RG8 normal + roughness) plus 2-3 atlas taps + 1-2 normal taps per fragment at close zoom is 3-6ms on SwiftShader by the proposer's own estimate. Stacked with water, AO, and bloom this can exceed the headless harness budget at the close band — the exact band the photoreal payoff lives in. ppm-gating the second octave is the right lever but the close band by definition can't gate it off.

Atlas seam bleed + texture thrash across manually-addressed tiles (no hardware wrap) is a real artifact source that needs padding + per-tile clamp math; mishandled it produces visible grid seams that scream 'tech demo' at close zoom.

cinematic-film proposes stripping ALL lighting/haze/altitude terms baked into topo.ts and moving them live — a large, invasive rewrite of the bake that risks breaking the strategic-band byte-faithful read the recovered judges spent the most effort protecting. High blast radius for the foundation phase.
verdicts.recommendedSpine: photoreal-drone is the spine. As an art director judging 'real Kunar aerial/drone footage that stays a legible chart at every LOD band,' it is the only proposal whose CENTERPIECE directly attacks attempt-1's actual worst frames — the close/tactical bands where the ground is a smeared ochre wash and the river is a dead stripe (verified in noon-close.png and dawn-close.png). Its move is the right one: DEMOTE the albedo bake from 'the image' to one input of five and RECOMPOSE the surface per-fragment from the sim's own arrays (the material-ID data spine) so the ground RESOLVES instead of upscaling. It is the most honest about its riskiest bet (detail-normals on a top-down ortho at noon) and has a true graceful-degrade floor (linear lighting + world-scale material albedo + AO already beat attempt-1 even if normals are cut entirely). Its phasing is shippable-and-better at every commit. Crucially, it keeps the strategic band — the one band attempt-1 already got right — provably unchanged by ppm-gating detail to zero and calibrating noon luma numerically. GRAFT THREE THINGS THE SPINE LACKS: (1) From asset-fidelity, the continuous HESCO berm + sprite cast-shadows + contact-AO grounding driven by the same skyState. perProposal.strengths: Technically the most correct and the most honest of the four, and the only one whose 10x is carried by a per-fragment surface RECOMPOSITION rather than a post-process filter. The data-spine is sound and verified-grade: u_landId as R8UI/usampler2D + texelFetch is WebGL2 core (I confirmed 32 texture units / 8192 max-tex under the actual --use-angle=swiftshader harness), and the texelFetch-parity unit test mirrors the existing heightAt parity discipline. Detail-normal raking in a world-up TBN is the correct, cheap call for a near-planar ortho surface — perturbing the existing forward-difference normalAt by an atlas RG normal is one normalize + one tap, and it is genuinely the highest-payoff-per-ms technique in any of the four decks. The HBAO bake is costed honestly: I computed it at 512^2 x 16 azimuths ~= 1.3e8 heightAt fetches, ~0.6x of ONE existing 1024^2 shadow rebake, so 'reuse the omnidirectional march, do it in the terrain worker, hide it behind the deploy loading bar' is real, not hand-waved. The proposal correctly DEMOTES the albedo bake to one input of five — that is the actual answer to attempt-1's `albedo*(0.34+0.95*shade)`, and it's the only deck that frames the leap that way. ppm-gating detail+second-octave to ~0 at strategic is a legibility floor enforced by construction, calibrated to a numeric noon-luma gate rather than a vibe. The riskiest-bet section is the most self-aware in the set: it names the noon-flattening failure of detail-normals on a top-down ortho camera and pre-commits a graceful degrade (lean on albedo+AO+roughness at noon; fall back to a 1-tap detail-height->normal-via-derivatives if atlas taps are too dear on SwiftShader; absolute floor = Phases 1+3 already beat attempt-1).
perProposal.fatalFlaws: No fatal flaw. Two real soft spots. (1) The 'deterministic CPU/one-shot GLSL bake' of the 16-tile PBR atlas (albedo+RG-normal+roughness) is the largest unmeasured load-time cost and the place most likely to slip — generating 16 tiles of FBM+worley at 1024-2048 with believable per-material micro-relief is non-trivial authoring, and the deck waves at 'CPU bake or one-time offscreen GLSL pass' without committing. (2) Per-fragment cost at CLOSE on the software rasterizer: 2-3 albedo taps + 1-2 normal taps + the two-octave world-scale sampling per frag is the honest budget worry; the stated 3-6ms on SwiftShader is plausible but is the one number I'd insist on measuring at Phase 3 before believing, because the harness runs 1440x900 at DPR=1 (~1.3M frags) and SwiftShader is a CPU rasterizer where every extra dependent texture tap is real ms.
mustFix: Phase 3 MUST ship with a measured SwiftShader per-frame number at CLOSE band (the matrix already does this) AND a hard atlas-tap budget — pre-decide the fallback (single detail-height tap -> derivative normals) as a compile flag, not a maybe.

Specify the manual per-tile atlas addressing math (clamp UV per tile, padded gutters) concretely — atlas bleed at tile seams under LINEAR_MIPMAP is the classic shipping bug and the deck only gestures at it.
Wire the new u_surfaceState into BOTH serialize() and loadWorld() if snow/wetness persist across save (invariant), or explicitly declare it a pure function of (clock,weather,seed) recomputed on load.

perProposal.strengths: The most coherent light-transport THESIS and the strongest single 'holy shit' frame (geometrically-true in-fog god-rays sampled from the SAME cast-shadow map the relief uses — that is the right, honest way to get shafts, and it reuses a resident texture). Moving to linear-HDR + real ACES is correct and, crucially, I VERIFIED the load-bearing assumption: under --use-angle=swiftshader, RGBA16F is renderable, EXT_color_buffer_float/half_float both report true, and OES_texture_float_linear is available — so the HDR foundation is NOT the risk the deck fears, and the RGBA8 packed-exposure fallback is a belt-and-suspenders nicety rather than a likely path. Single-scattering aerial perspective via a vertical-column approximation is the physically-right cheat for an ortho camera and is correctly costed as folding into the relief pass. The 'one shadow source, three consumers (relief, fog, god-ray mask), no fork' architecture is exactly how a staff engineer would wire it. P0 (HDR + computed light, no new data) is a genuinely safe first commit that already beats attempt-1.
perProposal.fatalFlaws: This is the deck most likely to blow the SwiftShader per-frame budget, and it under-weights that because it mis-identified its own top risk as RGBA16F renderability (a non-issue on the target) instead of FILL-RATE on a CPU rasterizer. The honest danger stack it signs up for is brutal on software: a 6-8 step fog raymarch where EVERY step does a heightAt (4 texelFetch) AND a cast-shadow sample, at screen res (~1.3M frags), PLUS a separate half-res 24-32-tap radial-blur god-ray pass, PLUS bright-pass + two-pass separable bloom, PLUS a screen-space sprite-relight pass, PLUS the tonemap/grade/grain pass. That is 5-6 fullscreen-ish passes layered on the one draw attempt-1 had. The stated ~0.9ms for the 8-tap fog 'when present' and ~0.7ms for the radial god-rays are iGPU-optimistic; on SwiftShader these are the items that turn a 16ms frame into a 60ms+ frame, and the deck's per-item ms estimates do not sum to an honest frame total anywhere. The screen-space god-ray pass (5b) is also the weakest GLSL: faking an on-screen sun-anchor for a sun geometrically BELOW the horizon at exactly the low-sun times shafts appear is a taste-and-correctness trap (shafts must rake from the true azimuth, and an off-screen virtual anchor with a Mitchell-decay radial blur is the classic cheesy-lens-flare failure).
mustFix: Publish an HONEST summed per-frame budget on SwiftShader for the WORST frame (dawn, fog present, low sun, close band = fog raymarch + god-rays + bloom + sprite-relight all firing) BEFORE P2 merges — not per-item ms in isolation. This is the gate the whole deck lives or dies on.

Make the fog raymarch step-count and the god-ray pass HARD-gated by a measured frame-time budget, not just by zoom/sun-altitude; pre-commit that 5b (screen-space radial god-rays) is cut to 5a-only (in-fog shafts) if the worst frame exceeds budget — the deck says this but must make it a numeric trigger.

Drop or de-scope the screen-space sprite-relight pass for v1: it is a whole extra fullscreen pass for the lowest-confidence payoff, and asset-fidelity's deck shows relighting sprites correctly is a much bigger problem (rotated-normal world-frame bug) than 'one screen-space tint' admits.
Keep the formLightNW noon guard verbatim and prove non-inversion numerically at noon before P1 merges (the deck commits to this; hold it to it).

perProposal.strengths: Picks the single most defensible 10x LEVER for a top-down COIN map: MOTION + WATER, the two things a real drone feed has that no static surface can fake. The flow-advected river (baked RG8 flow field from centerX gradient + R8 bank-distance mask, two scrolling normal octaves blended Vlachos-style, clock-keyed so it freezes on pause) is textbook-correct, deterministic, and masked to ~2-4% of pixels so the cost is honest. The whitewater-foam-at-fords idea is the best legibility WIN in the entire set — it makes the tactically-critical crossing MORE obvious while looking real, turning a 'go wild' effect into a gameplay aid. Weather-as-ground-STATE (wetness/snow accumulators integrated off the sim clock, persisted as floats in serialize+loadWorld) is the correct mechanism and correctly flags the both-functions invariant. The canopy-as-lit-material with a height bump injected into the EXISTING shadow march (so canopy throws shadows 'for free' in the same R8 rebake) is a clever, low-cost reuse. Phase plan is the most incremental and lowest-blast-radius (P1 tonemap+AO with zero new data, then the river as the headline), and the 'pause stills the water mid-glint' moment is a real, ownable demonstration of the master-clock thesis.
perProposal.fatalFlaws: The vegetation/canopy 10x is weaker and riskier than the water 10x and the deck leans on both equally. 'Canopy noise + relief shade fighting' is a real legibility hazard the deck admits but only mitigates by 'keep it a tinted modulation' — multi-octave canopy lobes lit by a micro-normal over the macro relief is exactly where the map turns to noise at operational zoom, and it's less self-aware about this than photoreal's noon-flattening analysis. The post chain (ACES + bloom + height-based AO) is correctly flagged as the cost risk, but like cinematic the deck doesn't sum an honest worst-frame total — and it stacks the water pass + canopy fbm taps + rain-pooling + the post chain. The smoke-occlusion hook couples the render layer to the live Effect list across the layer line; the deck routes it through the store correctly but it's the right thing to cut first (and it says so). The biggest gap vs photoreal: there is NO per-material PBR atlas, so at CLOSE zoom the NON-water, NON-canopy ground (scree, cropland, rock) still resolves toward attempt-1's single-fbm-grain-multiply — the deck's own words — so the close-zoom 'real surface' read is carried by water+canopy only, leaving large swaths of close-zoom ground still smeared.
mustFix: Add a per-material micro-detail term for the non-water/non-canopy ground at CLOSE (even a 1-tap detail-normal), or explicitly concede that close-zoom open ground stays attempt-1-grade — right now the deck implies a full close-zoom transform it doesn't deliver off the river/canopy.

Gate canopy lobe AMPLITUDE hard by ppm with a measured operational-band legibility screenshot proving forest-vs-open-ground separability does not degrade into noise (the deck names this; make it a merge gate).
Publish a summed worst-frame SwiftShader budget (water pass + canopy + rain pool + AO + bloom + tonemap firing together) before the post-chain phase merges; pre-commit bloom as the first cut.

Add wetness AND snow accumulator floats to BOTH serialize() and loadWorld() with a round-trip assertion in smoke.ts (the deck says this — hold it; a missed persisted float is the classic determinism-contract break).

perProposal.strengths: Correctly diagnoses the SINGLE biggest unaddressed 'icons-on-a-map' tell that the other three barely touch — the 164 flat SVG sprites, which the reference close/tactical frames confirm are the most game-y element on screen (the COP reads as stickers). The deferred-lit instanced sprite pass is architecturally the right move and is, as claimed, strictly CHEAPER than today's 164 individual CPU drawImage blits — one instanced draw vs 164 blits is a real win on the software path, and instancing is WebGL2 core. The rotated-normal-into-world-frame detail (rotate n.xy by the sprite's rot in the fragment, NOT bake-time) is the exact bug a staff engineer would catch on rotating soldiers/vehicles, and the deck both names it and proposes a turntable probe — the most surgically-correct GLSL insight in any deck. HESCO-as-one-continuous-extruded-berm (vs 60 identical rotated decals) is the highest-leverage single re-author for the COP. The 2D-fallback parity (albedo channel of the GBuffer IS the old flat sprite, single ok-flag branch mirroring TerrainGL.ok) is the most robust degradation story in the set. RGBA16F for its tonemap pass is safe (I verified renderability on the harness).
perProposal.fatalFlaws: It is the LEAST '10x of the TERRAIN' — the brief's literal mandate is the WebGL terrain route, and this deck spends its best ideas on assets while its terrain section (technique 9: a 26-row material LUT + detail-normals + animated water) is a thinner, bolted-on version of what photoreal/living-valley make their centerpiece. The named riskiest bet is the one most likely to collapse the value prop: SDF-extrude-from-silhouette producing convincing normals/AO for 164 assets WITHOUT hand-authoring is the 'puffed-pillow' failure mode, and the deck's own fallback concedes that only the ~20 hand-authored heroes will really read — i.e. the cheap-volume promise is the part most likely to not materialize, leaving a lot of assets still flat. The authoring load is the real schedule risk (height layers for ~20 heroes + a new bake stage in build-asset-manifest.mjs emitting a 4096^2 multi-channel atlas — ~8MB+ upload, the largest texture-memory line in any deck, and the deck states it loosely). Specular on a top-down ortho map is the per-frame flourish most likely to read as a tech-demo glint, and it's correctly flagged as first-to-cut. Net: the strongest IDEAS for the weakest target — it would make a phenomenal GRAFT onto a terrain spine but is the wrong backbone for a terrain-route mandate.
mustFix: Re-scope as an ADDITIVE asset campaign layered on a terrain spine, not a standalone terrain answer — the terrain material-LUT section must either match photoreal's atlas depth or explicitly defer to it; shipping a thin terrain layer here would re-commit attempt-1's timidity on the exact axis the owner called out.

Prove SDF-extrude gives non-mushy normals on 3-4 representative LONG-TAIL (non-hero) assets at tactical zoom BEFORE committing the bake pipeline; if it's pillow-y, pivot the long tail to cast-shadow-grounding + contact-AO only and say so up front.

State the atlas texture-memory budget concretely (4096^2 RGBA8 x how many channel-atlases = MB) and confirm it against the 8192 max-tex / upload cost; this is the largest unstated memory line in the set.

Keep the helo rotor disk and any wall-clock element strictly behind the screen-space-precip exemption, and verify the sprite cast-shadow Tier-2 height injection into the shadow FBO does not make tall-qalat shadows read as terrain in a paused still (the deck names this; gate it).

bestGrafts: photoreal-drone's per-landcover PBR material atlas + detail-normal raking is the single highest-payoff-per-ms technique in the entire fan-out and should be the close/tactical-zoom centerpiece of WHATEVER spine ships — it is the only proposal that actually answers 'the ground is an upscaled bitmap at close zoom' for ALL land classes, not just water/canopy.

photoreal-drone's baked horizon-angle HBAO field (omnidirectional reuse of the existing shadow march, done in the terrain worker, hidden behind the deploy loading bar) — I verified it's ~0.6x of one existing shadow rebake, near-free per-frame (one tap), and it's the contact-darkening every real orthophoto has. Graft into any spine.
living-valley's whitewater-foam-at-fords: the rare 'go wild' effect that INCREASES legibility (the SOP crossing becomes more obvious). Graft onto any water shader regardless of which deck owns water.

living-valley's flow-advected river (baked RG8 flow field from centerX gradient + bank-distance mask, two-octave Vlachos flowmap blend, clock-keyed) — the cleanest, most deterministic, most cost-honest water implementation across the three decks that propose water; prefer it over cinematic's and asset-fidelity's water descriptions.

cinematic-film's in-fog god-rays sampled from the existing cast-shadow map (technique 5a ONLY — NOT the screen-space radial pass 5b): geometrically true, reuses a resident texture, near-free, and carries the marquee dawn frame without the lens-flare risk. Graft 5a, drop 5b.

asset-fidelity's instanced deferred sprite pass with rotated-normal-into-WORLD-frame lighting + the HESCO-as-continuous-extruded-berm re-author: the correct and necessary answer to the flat-SVG 'stickers' tell, and strictly cheaper than today's 164 CPU blits. Graft as a SEPARATE phase after the terrain spine lands.

photoreal-drone's altitude x aspect snow accumulation/melt and wet-ground darkening as deterministic surfaceState integrated from clock+weather — cleaner framing than living-valley's equivalent; graft whichever, but persist the floats in serialize+loadWorld with a smoke round-trip assert.

cinematic-film's single-scattering aerial-perspective via a vertical-column approximation (extinction + sun-tinted inscatter keyed to the SACRED visibilityM) — the physically-right ortho cheat for valley depth, folds into the relief pass; graft over the flat altitude-haze mix() all four inherit from attempt-1.
legibilityTraps: NOON FLATTENING is the deepest trap and only photoreal-drone analyzes it rigorously: with the sun due-south on a north-up map, NdotL goes near-uniform across micro-facets exactly when detail-normals are supposed to carry close-zoom detail, so the surface can flatten back to 'painted' precisely at noon. ALL detail-normal decks must scale detailStrength DOWN with sun rake-angle and keep the formLightNW guard verbatim; verify non-inversion NUMERICALLY at noon at all 4 bands, not by eye.

CANOPY/MICRO-NORMAL vs MACRO-RELIEF noise at OPERATIONAL zoom: living-valley's lit canopy lobes and any per-material detail-normal can dissolve the form read into stipple at the band where terrain SHAPE must dominate. The fix is hard ppm-gating of detail AMPLITUDE (not just presence) with an operational-band forest-vs-open separability screenshot as a merge gate — every deck claims ppm-gating but only photoreal makes it a numeric floor.

HDR + ACES quietly LOWERS shadowed-face luminance: ACES desaturates and rolls highlights, but the toe can crush shadow detail below the legibility floor (contract #4). cinematic/living-valley/asset-fidelity all move to ACES; each must clamp the sky-fill/ambient floor so shadowed faces stay >= ~0.45x lit luma (sky.ts already specs shadowStrength for this) and PROVE it at dusk/night.

BLOOM veiling the tactical read: every deck adds threshold bloom. It is architecturally safe ONLY because HUD/contours/units are on the SEPARATE 2D canvas above the GL layer — but the GL terrain showing THROUGH gaps in symbology can still be veiled, washing draws/ridgelines used for LOS. Keep the threshold high (luma>=1.0 knee), bloom GL-only, and verify the strategic relief read survives bloom at golden hour.

cinematic-film's screen-space god-ray pass (5b) is a LEGIBILITY and taste trap: a faked off-screen sun-anchor with radial blur can rake bright streaks across the tactical center. The in-fog variant (5a) is safe; 5b must be center-protected or cut.

FOG/WET/SNOW burying the read: all decks add wet-darkening, snow whitening, raymarched/pooled fog. Each is a luminance shift that can stack with night + cloud-shadow + aerial-haze into a sub-floor frame. The single-fold weather rule (exposure carries weatherLightMult exactly once) must be preserved and the COMBINED worst case (Fog weather + night + heavy cloud) must be screenshot-gated, not reasoned about per-effect.
feasibilityTraps: THE BIGGEST STATED RISK IN THREE DECKS IS A NON-RISK ON THE TARGET: I probed the actual harness flag (--use-angle=swiftshader) and ANGLE-over-SwiftShader (Vulkan 1.3) reports EXT_color_buffer_float=true, EXT_color_buffer_half_float=true, OES_texture_float_linear=true, RGBA16F renderable=true, RGBA32F renderable=true, MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE=8192, 32 texture units. cinematic-film, living-valley, and asset-fidelity all spend their riskiest-bet budget worrying about RGBA16F renderability — it works. The probe-and-fallback to RGBA8-packed-exposure is good engineering but will NOT trigger on this harness. Conversely --disable-gpu returns NOGL (no WebGL2 at all), which is exactly why the alive-2D-fallback branch must be preserved.

THE REAL TRAP IS FILL-RATE ON A CPU RASTERIZER, NOT PRECISION. SwiftShader is software; precision is full-float (highp is already in the recovered shaders, so the 'low-precision strobe' worries are overstated). The honest danger is per-frame fullscreen passes: cinematic-film signs up for ~5-6 layered passes (screen-res fog raymarch with per-step cast-shadow + heightAt = up to 8*5 texture ops/frag, half-res 24-32-tap radial god-rays, 2-pass bloom, sprite-relight, tonemap) at 1440x900 DPR=1 (~1.3M frags). NO deck publishes a SUMMED worst-frame budget — they list per-item ms that are iGPU-optimistic and never add up. This is the universal must-fix: an honest worst-frame total on SwiftShader before the heavy phase merges.

RAYMARCHED PER-FRAME FOG is the costliest honest item: cinematic's 6-8 step fog where each step does heightAt (4 texelFetch) + a cast-shadow tap is ~32-40 dependent texture ops per fog fragment per frame on a CPU rasterizer. The early-out (skip if fragElev>fogTop) saves clear days but the dawn-fog marquee frame is precisely when it's most expensive. Must be step-count-LOD'd AND frame-budget-gated.

ATLAS/GBUFFER TEXTURE MEMORY is understated: photoreal's 2048^2 PBR atlas + normal atlas + control textures, and asset-fidelity's 4096^2 multi-channel GBuffer atlas (~8MB+), are the largest unstated memory and upload-cost lines. 8192 max-tex is fine, but upload time and the seed-determinism of procedurally-generated atlases (photoreal) need a hash assertion in smoke.ts.

SHADOW-MARCH REUSE IS GENUINELY CHEAP, AND THE DECKS THAT LEAN ON IT ARE RIGHT: the recovered SHADOW_FRAG is 56 steps x 4 texelFetch, rebaked only on sun motion (~once/game-min at 1x). photoreal's HBAO (16-azimuth omnidirectional march at 512^2) is ~0.6x ONE shadow rebake (I computed 1.3e8 vs 2.35e8 heightAt fetches) and is a load-time/worker cost, not per-frame — this is the rare honest cost claim. living-valley's canopy-height-bump into the same march is also legitimately near-free.

DETERMINISM/PERSISTED-STATE TRAP: living-valley and photoreal both add accumulator floats (wetness, snow depth). Every persisted float MUST land in BOTH serialize() and loadWorld() with a smoke.ts round-trip assert, or it's a determinism-contract break (a same-seed run that diverges). The decks say this; it is the easiest invariant to silently miss across a 7-9 phase plan.
verdicts.recommendedSpine: "SPINE = photoreal-drone, with grafts. It is the only proposal whose 10x is a genuine per-fragment surface RECOMPOSITION (albedo demoted to one input of five) rather than parity-plus-a-post-filter, it is the most technically correct and the most cost-honest (its HBAO and shadow-reuse cost claims survived my fetch-count math; its riskiest-bet section is the only one that correctly identifies its own true failure mode — noon flattening — and pre-commits a graceful degrade), and its phase plan keeps the game green-and-better at every commit with P1 (linear lighting + ACES, no new data) already beating attempt-1. It directly answers the owner's exact grievance: attempt-1 was a flat painted bitmap with a tint, and photoreal is the only deck that makes the GROUND ITSELF resolve into real per-material surface for ALL land classes at close zoom. Onto that spine, graft: (1) living-valley's flow-advected river + whitewater-foam-at-fords as the water marquee (cleaner and more legibility-positive than photoreal's own water section); (2) cinematic-film's in-fog god-rays (5a ONLY) sampled from the existing shadow map for the dawn marquee frame, and its single-scattering aerial-perspective for valley depth — but explicitly DROP cinematic's screen-space god-ray pass (5b), its multi-pass HDR ambition, and its sprite-relight pass, which together are the fill-rate trap that no honest SwiftShader budget survives; (3) asset-fidelity's instanced deferred sprite pass + HESCO-continuous-berm as a LATER, SEPARATE asset campaign after the terrain spine ships — it is the correct answer to the flat-SVG 'stickers' tell (visible in the reference close/tactical frames) but is the wrong backbone for a terrain-route mandate and would re-commit attempt-1's timidity if it owned the terrain. CROSS-CUTTING GATE for the merged spine: publish a SUMMED worst-frame SwiftShader budget (dawn + fog + low-sun + close, all effects firing) before any heavy phase merges — the universal weakness across all four decks is per-item ms estimates that never add up, and the real risk is CPU-rasterizer fill-rate, not the RGBA16F renderability they all feared (which I verified works on the actual --use-angle=swiftshader harness)."

perProposal.strengths: This is a genuine transformation, not parity-plus-a-filter: it demotes the albedo bake from 'the image' to one of five inputs and recomposes the surface per-fragment from a per-material PBR atlas. From a legibility standpoint its single best move is that the transformation is BUILT to collapse gracefully toward the byte-faithful read at strategic zoom: detail-normals, the atlas second octave, bloom and procedural decoration are all ppm-gated to ~0 below ppm 0.5, calibrated to attempt-1's noon luma as a NUMERIC gate (not a vibe). That means STRATEGIC is provably the legible relief+contours map of today — the highest-stakes band for command reading is protected by construction, not by taste. The legibilityPlan is the most rigorous of the four: it names the exact bands, keeps the `formLightNW` relief-inversion blend (which the recovered shader confirms at shaders.ts:138-142, the load-bearing noon guard), scales detailStrength DOWN as the sun flattens, and the HBAO (multiplying the AMBIENT term, never the direct) is form-REVEALING — it darkens draw-bottoms and cliff bases, which deepens the tactical read of where the dead ground is rather than burying it. AO is the one effect in the whole set that makes terrain MORE legible. Cast-shadow penumbra reuse of the proven 56-step march keeps the marquee multi-km dawn ridge shadow that carries the operational read.
perProposal.fatalFlaws: The riskiest bet (which the proposal honestly flags) is a direct legibility threat at the worst possible time. The photoreal trigger is 'the low sun rakes micro-normals into facets' — but at NOON the real sun is due south and near-vertical (sun-probe asserts noon vector ~(0,0.24,0.97)), so NdotL is near-uniform across all micro-facets and the surface flattens back toward 'painted' exactly at the band-agnostic legibility-critical time. Worse: the `formLightNW` guard at noon lights the MACRO relief with a FAKED NW key (max(keySun,keyNW)), so if detail-normals are lit by the real south sun while the macro form is lit by a fake NW key, the micro and macro light disagree — pebble-shadows point one way, the slope-shading points another, which reads as noise laid over relief rather than coherent surface. The proposal's mitigation (detailStrength scales with sun-rake-angle so noon leans on albedo+AO) is correct but means the close-zoom 'holy shit' surface is WEAKEST at noon — the one time of day with no atmosphere to hide behind. Second trap: per-material detail-normals on cropland 'furrows running along the contour' is a directional high-frequency pattern that at tactical zoom can be mistaken for micro-terrain or for a man-made feature (a wall, a wadi) the player must read — a furrow texture that looks like a defilade line is a tactical-read failure. Third: the wet-ground specular sheen and water glint, if they land on or near a route/ford, add a bright moving highlight exactly where the player reads crossing tactics; capped, but a noon wet-sheen over a road is a glare risk the plan under-specifies.
mustFix: At noon specifically, gate detail-normals to near-zero AND drive the micro-normal light direction from the SAME faked NW key the macro `formLightNW` guard uses, so micro and macro shading never disagree — verify with a noon close-zoom squint at all 4 bands against attempt-1's noon frames as the numeric gate.

Cap cropland furrow-normal amplitude and forbid furrow direction from aligning with contour lines tightly enough to be mistaken for a defilade/wall — a tactical-feature-confusion screenshot probe (furrowed cropland adjacent to a real wadi) must show they read as distinct.

Hard-clamp wet-ground specular and water glint so no bright highlight ever lands on a road/trail/ford route at any sun angle; gate the wet sheen by sunIntensity so it self-limits under overcast (when it's actually wet) — and screenshot a wet-noon-clear edge case to prove no route glare.

Snow coverage must be capped BELOW ridgelines used for LOS (proposal says this) — add an explicit metric: ridge-cells that are skyline/LOS-relevant never exceed a snow-albedo threshold that would wash the crest silhouette the player ranges off.

perProposal.strengths: The HDR-linear + ACES foundation is a real transformation and the right one — attempt-1 wrote raw clamped linear and the golden-hour highlights clip flat; a real tonemap is the single change that lets the dynamic range of dawn be legible rather than crushed. Moving aerial perspective and fog from `mix(col,fogColor,t)` paint to actual single-scattering light transport is physically honest and is the correct depth cue for a 2km valley. The discipline of ONE cast-shadow source feeding three consumers (relief, fog raymarch, god-ray mask) is clean architecture that keeps the shadows geometrically TRUE — god-rays that rake from the real sun azimuth are at least honest, not arbitrary. The two-canvas firewall is correctly invoked (the grade lives entirely in the GL pass; the 2D symbology canvas is physically untouched), and the noon auto-vanish logic (inscatter keyed to terminator, fog burns off by 10:00, god-rays gated by 1-sunUp) means the cinematic effects correctly DISAPPEAR at noon, which is the right instinct.
perProposal.fatalFlaws: This is the highest legibility risk in the entire set, and the danger lands squarely on the two effects it calls its marquee. (1) RAYMARCHED VALLEY FOG: the reference `fog-dawn-operational.png` is ALREADY at the legibility floor — the valley floor is heavily veiled and terrain is barely readable. Replacing the capped `mix()` veil with an inscatter ACCUMULATION that can exceed the old veil, then ADDING bloom on the lit fog, risks pushing the floor below readable exactly in the river draw — the most tactically important ground (the approach, the crossing). The cap (inscatter ≤0.55) is asserted but inscatter+bloom+aerial-perspective COMPOUND, and the plan never proves the worst-case sum stays above the floor. (2) GOD-RAYS: the proposal itself admits this is 'highest taste risk... most prone to reading as a cheesy lens-flare game effect,' requires FAKING an on-screen sun-anchor for a sun geometrically below the horizon, and the screen-space radial-blur pass (5b) is a screen-space veil that fans bright streaks ACROSS the frame — directly over terrain the player is reading. A radial-blur light-shaft pass is the textbook way to bury a tactical read under a glow. (3) FILM FINISH: chromatic aberration and vignette, even 'corner-only,' degrade edge legibility — and the operational/strategic bands put terrain at the corners. Grain over a relief map adds high-frequency noise the eye must filter from real micro-relief. (4) SPRITE RELIGHT via a screen-space directional gradient keyed to spriteShadow risks lighting rotating sprites (soldiers/vehicles) with a light that spins with them — the exact bug the art-seam review flagged — unless the normal is in world frame, which a screen-space gradient is NOT. The cinematic ambition is real but it spends its budget on the three effects (fog, god-rays, film finish) most hostile to a tactical instrument.
mustFix: Prove the COMPOUND worst case: aerial-perspective inscatter + fog inscatter + bloom, summed at dawn-fog in the river draw, must stay above an explicit luma legibility floor measured against `fog-dawn-operational.png` — a single numeric gate, not three independent caps. If the sum buries the draw, the fog raymarch must be alpha-clamped as one combined veil.

Cut the screen-space god-ray pass (5b) by default — keep ONLY the in-fog shafts (5a), which are geometrically honest and self-limited by fog density. The screen-space radial pass fans bright streaks over readable terrain and is the single most likely effect to fail the legibility contract; make it opt-in behind a numeric review gate, not the default.

Drop chromatic aberration entirely (it degrades the edge read where operational/strategic terrain lives) and make vignette a no-op above operational ppm. Gate grain to OFF under the screenshot harness AND keep amplitude below the micro-relief detail floor so it can't be mistaken for terrain texture.

Sprite relight must rotate the normal into WORLD frame per-sprite (not a screen-space gradient keyed to a fixed shadow direction) or rotating soldiers/vehicles get lighting that spins with heading — verify with a turntable probe of a single soldier rotating through 360°.

perProposal.strengths: The thesis — that a top-down drone feed reads as alive through MOTION and WATER, not a prettier static surface — is correct and is a real transformation. From a legibility angle its standout move is that the animated river makes the tactical read BETTER: foam blooming and advecting at fords and steep channel cells turns 'where do I cross' into a visibly churning, more-obvious cue (the proposal explicitly notes the foam lands exactly where the SOP says to cross). Water that is mask-gated to river cells can never bleed onto tactical ground — a clean construction guarantee. The Fresnel reflection is the SKY color (already a legible, calibrated value), and at strategic zoom the river still reads as a coherent blue thread because detail amplitude scales with ppm. The wetness/snow accumulators are LUMINANCE shifts inside the locked palette — never occluders — so weather-as-material can't bury the read the way volumetric fog can. The phasing is the most incremental and lowest-risk of the four (tonemap+AO first as cheap must-keeps, water as the headline, bloom as a cut-able add-on), and it correctly reuses the `formLightNW` guard verbatim for noon.
perProposal.fatalFlaws: Three legibility traps, none fatal but real. (1) MOTION introduces a NEW read-ambiguity the static proposals don't have: canopy sway and grass shimmer at tactical zoom risk a 'seasick' read, and more subtly, MOTION on the map competes for attention with the things that SHOULD move — units, fire, threat cues on the 2D layer. A stirring forest can pull the eye off a moving contact. The amplitude+ppm cap is asserted but the attention-competition between world-motion and tactical-motion is not addressed. (2) RAIN POOLING in the draw via the local-floor field routes low-lying fragments through the water BRDF — this paints reflective water onto ground that is normally readable terrain, and the player must not mistake a transient rain pool for a permanent water feature or for the river itself. 'Pools in dead ground, never on routes' is asserted but the local-floor field is coarse (128²) and the draw IS often the approach route. (3) SNOW accumulation by slope/altitude that lerps albedo→white with a STRONG sky-ambient bounce filling shadow is the classic way to WASH a crest — snow that fills shadow with cold light flattens the very relief the player ranges off; the proposal claims 'snow reveals form beautifully' but cold-bounce fill into shadow does the opposite of revealing form. (4) Smoke-occlusion coupling the render to the live Effect list crosses the layer line if done carelessly; flagged cut-safe, which is correct.
mustFix: Add an explicit motion budget: canopy/grass sway amplitude must be below the threshold where it competes with tactical motion (units/fire) for attention, and gate sway to OFF at operational and strategic — verify by A/B screenshotting a moving contact over a still vs swaying forest and confirming the contact still reads first.

Rain pools must be visually distinct from the permanent river/fords (different desaturation/edge treatment) so a transient pool is never mistaken for a water feature, and must NOT route any route/trail cell through the water BRDF — clamp pooling to true basins only and screenshot a rain-on-approach-route edge case.

Snow's shadow-fill bounce must be capped so it never raises shadowed crest faces above the lit-face luma (which would invert/flatten the silhouette the player ranges off) — keep contours dark-over-snow (the plan says this) and add a snow-noon-strategic squint gate proving the ridgeline silhouette survives.

Keep smoke-occlusion strictly read-only via the store marshalling Effect positions into a texture (engine stays React-free); ship it last and cut-first if it muddies the sun-beam read or couples layers.

perProposal.strengths: This is the most legibility-SAFE proposal in the set because its transformation lives on OBJECTS (sprites/structures), gated through a single audited `u_detailGain` uniform that crossfades ALL added detail (specular, detail-normals, sprite-lighting, bloom) to zero at strategic, where sprites become the existing screen-fixed NATO symbols via the untouched lodAlpha path — so pulling out ALWAYS yields a clean chart. The strategic-fallback (its own technique #15) is framed correctly as a CONTRACT, not an effect: it REDUCES work when zoomed out and is the guardrail that lets everything else go wild. Lit sprites under the same SkyState as the terrain is the right unification — ONE sun drives relief, cast shadows, sprite lighting, water, grade — so the frame moves as one coherent lit world. The contact/aerial-AO that grounds objects in the dirt is a pure legibility WIN (a building that sits IN the ground reads as a real structure, not a floating icon). Extending `formLightNW` from terrain to sprites is the correct noon guard for the new lit sprites. The 2D-fallback parity (shares the albedo atlas) means the worst case is 'today's look plus a grade,' never broken. Most disciplined legibility plan of the four.
perProposal.fatalFlaws: It is NOT a 10x of the BRIEF's stated target. The mandate is 'photoreal drone/satellite feed of a VALLEY' and 'level up ALL visuals' — but this proposal's center of gravity is the COP and the 164 sprites, with terrain materials/water bolted on (techniques 9-10) almost as an afterthought. The valley itself — the thing a drone feed is OF — gets the least transformative treatment. The owner reverted attempt-1 for being timid about the GROUND; this risks being timid about the ground in a different way (it transforms the furniture, not the room). Two real legibility risks remain. (1) LIT ROTATING SPRITES: the marquee deferred pass must rotate the tangent-space normal into WORLD frame AFTER the sprite's rot, or every soldier/vehicle gets lighting that spins with heading — the proposal flags this as the exact bug to verify, which is honest, but it is the single most common way lit sprites break. (2) VEHICLE/SOLDIER SPECULAR on a top-down ortho map: a metal hood-glint that 'slides as the sun moves' is precisely the 'tech-demo glint' that reads as game-y and can draw the eye to a parked truck over a live threat; the proposal makes it the first cut, correctly. The marquee 'continuous HESCO berm' is also only a partial win — the pre-WebGL reference (02-cop-tactical.png) ALREADY renders HESCO as a continuous berm; it is attempt-1's WebGL path that regressed it to dotted segments, so this is recovering a regression as much as a 10x leap.
mustFix: Rebalance toward the VALLEY: the terrain-material + water + canopy techniques (9-12) must be promoted from afterthought to co-headline, or this fails the brief's 'drone feed of a valley' bar even if the COP is gorgeous — the owner reverted timidity about the GROUND.

Rotate sprite normals into world frame per-instance in the fragment (verified with a 360° turntable probe of one soldier) so rotating units never get heading-spun lighting — this is the load-bearing correctness gate for the entire deferred pass.

Cap and gate vehicle/glass specular hard (first cut): a sliding metal glint must never out-compete a live threat cue for attention at tactical zoom — A/B a parked MRAP glint vs a contact marker and confirm the threat reads first.

Verify the SDF-extrude-from-silhouette baseline doesn't produce 'puffed-pillow' samey lighting that makes distinct asset classes (qalat vs B-hut vs TOC) harder to tell apart at operational zoom — class-distinctness is a tactical read; screenshot a mixed village+COP at operational and confirm building types remain distinguishable.

bestGrafts: The two-canvas legibility firewall (all four converge on it): contours/units/reticles/labels/HUD stay on the transparent ungraded 2D canvas ABOVE the GL layer, physically untouchable by any shader. This is the architectural guarantee that lets the GL layer 'go wild' — make it the explicit, non-negotiable spine of the whole effort.

photoreal-drone's single audited ppm-gate that collapses ALL added detail toward the byte-faithful strategic read, calibrated to attempt-1's noon luma as a NUMERIC gate (not a vibe). Combine with asset-fidelity's framing of this as a single `u_detailGain` CONTRACT uniform every technique multiplies through — one audited lever protects the strategic-band read by construction.
